subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the consequence if a transport vehicle operates without a valid certificate of fitness under Section 56?

options.A: It is charged double toll charges
options.B: It is deemed to be an unregistered vehicle under Section 39 and punishable under Section 192
options.C: It is allowed 30 days grace period

explanation: Since Section 56(1) states the vehicle is not deemed to be validly registered without fitness, driving it amounts to driving an unregistered vehicle under Section 39.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Rule 62 of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (as amended), what is the validity of the Certificate of Fitness for a newly registered transport vehicle?

options.A: 1 year
options.B: 5 years
options.C: 2 years

explanation: Under CMV Rule 62 (as amended), the initial fitness certificate for a new transport vehicle is valid for 2 years, and subsequently renewable every year (or 2 years up to 8 years for certain classes).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a Certificate of Fitness under Section 56 be issued or renewed by an authorized automated testing station (ATS)?

options.A: No, only RTO officers can issue fitness certificates
options.B: Only for adapted two-wheelers
options.C: Yes, as provided under Section 56(1) and Central Motor Vehicles Rules
options.D: Only if police department endorses the certificate

explanation: Section 56 specifically provides for testing and issuance of fitness certificates by authorized testing stations.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56(4), a certificate of fitness may be cancelled at any time by a prescribed authority if:

options.A: The driver does not wear uniform
options.B: The vehicle no longer complies with all the requirements of the Act and Rules
options.C: The vehicle carries less than full load
options.D: The vehicle is parked in a private garage

explanation: Section 56(4) empowers the authority to cancel fitness if the vehicle no longer complies with statutory requirements.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What happens to the certificate of registration when a Certificate of Fitness is cancelled under Section 56(4)?

options.A: Registration is upgraded to national permit
options.B: Registration is suspended until a fresh certificate of fitness is obtained
options.C: Registration is automatically converted to private car

explanation: Under Section 56(4), cancellation of fitness certificate suspends the registration until a fresh fitness certificate is obtained.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 46, if an owner brings a vehicle registered in Tamil Nadu to Kerala for temporary use not exceeding 12 months:

options.A: The vehicle must be re-registered within 7 days
options.B: No fresh registration in Kerala is required
options.C: The registration is invalid immediately
options.D: The vehicle must be impounded under Section 207

explanation: Under Section 46 read with Section 47, registration remains effective throughout India; re-registration is required only if kept in another state for more than 12 months.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 47 of the MV Act, 1988, when is an owner required to apply for a new registration mark in another State?

options.A: If vehicle is kept for more than 6 months
options.B: If vehicle is kept for more than 30 days
options.C: If vehicle is kept for more than 60 days
options.D: If vehicle is kept in that other State for a period exceeding 12 months

explanation: Section 47 requires assignment of a new registration mark if the vehicle is kept in another state for more than 12 months.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 52(2), an alteration in a motor vehicle may be permitted for adapted vehicles to enable use by:

options.A: Persons under 18 years of age
options.B: Persons with disabilities
options.C: Driving school instructors

explanation: Section 52(2) provides that alterations may be made to enable use by a person with disability.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 52(3), can an owner change the engine of a motor vehicle?

options.A: No, engine change is strictly prohibited in India
options.B: Yes, but only with an identical second-hand engine without informing RTO
options.C: Yes, with prior approval of the registering authority subject to Central Government rules
options.D: Yes, but only if the engine has greater cubic capacity

explanation: Section 52 permits replacement of engine with prior approval of registering authority and compliance with emission norms.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 53(2), if an authority other than the original registering authority suspends a vehicle's registration, it must:

options.A: Destroy the certificate of registration immediately
options.B: Intimate the fact of suspension to the original registering authority
options.C: Forward the vehicle to the Central Government
options.D: Levy a separate state tax penalty

explanation: Section 53(2) mandates that the authority suspending registration shall intimate the fact of suspension to the original registering authority.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 55(2), if a motor vehicle is permanently removed out of India, who must be notified within 14 days?

options.A: The Ministry of External Affairs
options.B: The Reserve Bank of India
options.C: The registering authority

explanation: Under Section 55(2), the owner shall report permanent removal out of India to the registering authority within 14 days for cancellation of registration.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 55(3), if a vehicle has been destroyed or permanently incapacitated and owner fails to report within 14 days, the authority may cancel registration after:

options.A: Compulsorily auctioning the chassis
options.B: Filing criminal FIR in Supreme Court
options.C: Seizing the owner's bank accounts
options.D: Giving the owner an opportunity to explain or show cause

explanation: The authority must give the owner an opportunity to make representation before cancelling under Section 55(3).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56(2), a certificate of fitness shall remain effective:

options.A: Only on National Highways
options.B: Only within the district of issuance
options.C: Only within the home State

explanation: Subject to conditions, a certificate of fitness issued under Section 56 is effective throughout India.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which Section of MV Act, 1988 deals with 'Necessity for registration'?

options.A: Section 19
options.B: Section 39
options.C: Section 66

explanation: Section 39 deals with the necessity for registration.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which Section of the MV Act, 1988 empowers the authority to require production of a vehicle at the time of registration?

options.A: Section 41
options.B: Section 42
options.C: Section 44

explanation: Section 44 governs production of vehicle at the time of registration.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which Section deals with 'Certificate of fitness of transport vehicles'?

options.A: Section 48
options.B: Section 52
options.C: Section 65

explanation: Section 56 governs Certificate of fitness of transport vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 53, who among the following can suspend the registration of a motor vehicle?

options.A: Only the District Collector
options.B: Any traffic police constable
options.C: A registering authority or other prescribed authority

explanation: Section 53 empowers the registering authority or other prescribed authority (such as Joint RTO/RTO).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 52, fitting wider tyres and modified suspension altering the vehicle width beyond manufacturer specifications is:

options.A: Permitted if approved by local mechanic
options.B: Illegal and amounts to an unauthorized alteration under Section 52
options.C: Permitted on payment of Green Tax

explanation: Structural modifications altering specifications beyond manufacturer limits violate Section 52.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56(3), what document is issued when a fitness certificate is refused or vehicle is found defective during testing?

options.A: Temporary fitness permit
options.B: Notice specifying the defects and temporary permit/extension to remedy defects
options.C: Immediate confiscation memo

explanation: Under Section 56(3) and CMV Rules, a defect slip / notice specifying the defects is issued allowing time to rectify.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a commercial vehicle is fitted with an unapproved retrofitted CNG kit, which section of MV Act is violated?

options.A: Section 44
options.B: Section 46
options.C: Section 52

explanation: Retrofitting without compliance with prescribed standards violates Section 52.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 39, driving a motor vehicle without registration mark displayed in prescribed manner is an offence punishable under:

options.A: Section 177
options.B: Section 181
options.C: Section 185

explanation: Driving an unregistered vehicle under Section 39 is punishable under Section 192 of the MV Act.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 55, if an authority cancels the registration of a vehicle, the owner must:

options.A: Publish an advertisement in a national newspaper
options.B: Destroy the RC by burning
options.C: Transfer the RC to another vehicle
options.D: Surrender the certificate of registration to the authority

explanation: On cancellation of registration under Section 55, the owner must surrender the certificate of registration.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 44, can a registering authority inspect the vehicle at the premises of the dealer before registration?

options.A: Only if ordered by Supreme Court
options.B: No, inspection can only happen at RTO office
options.C: No, inspection is not allowed before sale
options.D: Yes, if authorized under prescribed rules and electronic inspection systems

explanation: Under modern rules and automated dealer-point registration under Section 44, inspection and verification can occur at authorized dealer premises.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 53(1), if a transport vehicle is found carrying passengers in excess of permitted capacity, can registration be suspended?

options.A: No, excess passengers is only a minor fine
options.B: Yes, if used in contravention of permit conditions or causing danger to public
options.C: Only if passengers lodge written complaint

explanation: Under Section 53(1), if used in a manner causing danger to public or in breach of permit conditions, registration can be suspended.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum penalty for altering a motor vehicle in contravention of Section 52 under Section 182A(4)?

options.A: Fine of Rs 1,000
options.B: Fine of Rs 5,000 per alteration
options.C: Imprisonment up to 6 months and/or fine of Rs 5,000 for owner, or fine of Rs 1,00,000 on manufacturer/dealer

explanation: Under Section 182A(4), making unauthorized alterations carries imprisonment up to 6 months and fine of Rs 5,000 on person altering, and up to Rs 1 lakh on dealers.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 46, how many registration certificates are required for a motor vehicle to operate across different States of India?

options.A: Two certificates: home State and inter-State
options.B: One for each State traversed
options.C: Separate registration for Southern and Northern States
options.D: Only one single valid registration certificate

explanation: Section 46 provides single pan-India effectiveness: only one registration is required.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56(5), the testing station inspecting vehicles for fitness must be:

options.A: Owned by a political party
options.B: Authorized by the State Government or Central Government as per prescribed norms
options.C: Any local tyre repair shop

explanation: Under Section 56, authorized testing stations must meet specifications and be accredited/authorized as per rules.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a private non-transport vehicle (such as a personal car) be subjected to fitness certification under Section 56?

options.A: No, Section 56 applies only to transport vehicles
options.B: Yes, Section 56 applies equally to all private and commercial vehicles at all times
options.C: Private cars need fitness renewal after 15 years as part of registration renewal under Section 41
options.D: Both A and C are legally correct descriptions

explanation: Section 56 applies strictly to 'transport vehicles'. Non-transport vehicles obtain fitness renewal as part of registration renewal after 15 years under Section 41.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 52, converting a passenger petrol car to run on battery electric power is:

options.A: Completely illegal and punishable with arrest
options.B: Permitted subject to approval of retrofitment kit by an approved testing agency and endorsement in RC
options.C: Permitted without informing any authority

explanation: Electric retrofitment is legally permitted under Section 52 provided the retrofit kit is type-approved and endorsed in RC.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If an owner replaces the damaged original body of a truck with a body of different dimensions not conforming to CMV Rules, the registering authority shall:

options.A: Issue a revised fitness certificate unconditionally
options.B: Refuse registration/fitness and take action under Section 52 and Section 53
options.C: Reward the owner for innovation
options.D: Transfer the vehicle to military transport

explanation: Non-conforming body modification violates Section 52 and CMV Rules, leading to refusal and action under Section 53.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 53(3), during the period of suspension of registration, the owner MUST:

options.A: Keep driving on secondary roads
options.B: Park the vehicle on national highway
options.C: Surrender the certificate of registration to the registering authority

explanation: Section 53(3) requires the owner to surrender the certificate of registration during the period of suspension.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 55(4), if a registering authority cancels registration, it shall communicate the cancellation to:

options.A: All village panchayats
options.B: Only the nearest police station
options.C: The tyre manufacturer
options.D: The owner and the original registering authority (if registered elsewhere)

explanation: Under Section 55(4), the authority cancelling registration must communicate it to the owner and original registering authority.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56(1), fitness certificate is required for:

options.A: All cycles and carts
options.B: Every transport vehicle
options.C: Only vehicles exceeding 25 tonnes
options.D: Only vehicles operating outside home district

explanation: Section 56(1) mandates fitness certificate for every transport vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory consequence under Section 56 if an authorized testing station issues a false fitness certificate?

options.A: The vehicle owner is held solely liable
options.B: No action can be taken as testing is private
options.C: Only a verbal warning
options.D: The station's approval may be cancelled and criminal/financial penalties applied under Section 182A

explanation: Issuing fraudulent fitness certificates leads to cancellation of authorization and penalties under Section 182A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 39, can a state government exempt any vehicle from registration?

options.A: Yes, all municipal vehicles are exempt from registration
options.B: Yes, State Government can exempt all commercial vehicles from registration
options.C: Yes, any vehicle older than 20 years is automatically exempt
options.D: No, exemptions are only as provided in the Act itself (e.g. dealer vehicles with TC)

explanation: Section 39 is mandatory; only specific statutory exemptions under the Act apply.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 52, fitting bull bars / crash guards in front of a passenger car:

options.A: Is mandatory for safety
options.B: Is illegal and violates Section 52 and CMV Rule 125H
options.C: Is allowed if made of aluminium

explanation: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) and High Courts held crash guards/bull bars illegal under Section 52.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 53, an appeal against an order of suspension of registration lies to:

options.A: The Supreme Court directly
options.B: The prescribed appellate authority within the prescribed time
options.C: The local municipal council

explanation: Under Section 57, an appeal against an order under Section 53 or 55 lies to the prescribed appellate authority.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 44, production of a vehicle can be dispensed with if:

options.A: The owner is an influential person
options.B: A certificate is produced from an authorized testing station or prescribed inspection agency
options.C: The vehicle is painted green

explanation: Under Section 44 and CMV Rules, physical production may be dispensed with on production of prescribed test/inspection certificates.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 55(1), if a vehicle is stolen and untraced for a long period, registration may be cancelled upon report from:

options.A: Pawn broker
options.B: Neighbouring car dealer
options.C: Local bank
options.D: Insurance company or police untraced report

explanation: Registration may be cancelled on based on police untraced final report and owner/insurer application.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56(4), if a fitness certificate is cancelled in another state, the inspecting officer shall report the fact to:

options.A: The vehicle driver's family
options.B: The Prime Minister's Office
options.C: Only the nearest toll plaza
options.D: The authority that issued the fitness certificate and the registering authority

explanation: Section 56(4) requires reporting the cancellation to the issuing authority.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 52, which modification is allowed for a person with disability?

options.A: Increasing engine speed beyond governor limit
options.B: Installing illegal tinted glass below 10% VLT
options.C: Removing all silencer mufflers
options.D: Fitting hand-operated accelerator and brake controls

explanation: Section 52(2) permits adapting vehicle controls (such as hand controls) for persons with disabilities.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 56 certificate of fitness is in which prescribed Form under Central Motor Vehicles Rules?

options.A: Form 20
options.B: Form 23
options.C: Form 38

explanation: Certificate of Fitness is issued in Form 38 under CMV Rules.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a registering authority suspend registration under Section 53 if a vehicle is repeatedly caught without PUC certificate?

options.A: Only after vehicle completes 15 years
options.B: No, PUC has no relation to vehicle registration
options.C: Only if fine exceeds Rs 1 lakh
options.D: Yes, as it fails to comply with the requirements of Chapter VII (safe and emission-compliant maintenance)

explanation: Non-compliance with Chapter VII emission standards under Section 53(1)(a) justifies suspension of registration.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 39, who is held liable if an unregistered vehicle is driven on a road?

options.A: Only the driver
options.B: Both the person driving and the owner who causes or permits the driving
options.C: Only the registering authority

explanation: Section 39 prohibits both driving by any person and causing/permitting driving by the owner.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 56, if a transport vehicle's fitness expires, how is it treated on the road?

options.A: It can ply on state highways but not national highways
options.B: It is treated as a private car
options.C: It is given 6 months automatic extension
options.D: It is treated as having no valid registration

explanation: Section 56(1) states it shall not be deemed validly registered without a valid fitness certificate.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, no owner of a motor vehicle shall use or permit the use of the vehicle as a transport vehicle in any public place:

options.A: Without paying local municipal toll
options.B: Save in accordance with the conditions of a permit granted or countersigned by a Regional or State Transport Authority
options.C: Unless it has at least 8 wheels
options.D: Unless driver is over 35 years of age

explanation: Section 66(1) requires a permit granted or countersigned by a Regional or State Transport Authority for using a transport vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(1), does the requirement of a permit apply when a transport vehicle is actually carrying NO passengers or goods?

options.A: No, empty vehicles never require a permit
options.B: Yes, whether or not such vehicle is actually carrying any passengers or goods
options.C: Only if empty vehicle travels at night
options.D: Only if empty vehicle exceeds 10 tonnes

explanation: Section 66(1) explicitly states: 'whether or not such vehicle is actually carrying any passengers or goods'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which of the following vehicles is EXEMPTED from the necessity of permits under Section 66(3)(a)?

options.A: All multi-axle goods trucks
options.B: All private luxury tourist buses
options.C: All auto-rickshaws operating in capital city
options.D: Any transport vehicle owned by Central Government or State Government and used for government purposes unconnected with any commercial enterprise

explanation: Section 66(3)(a) exempts transport vehicles owned by Central or State Government used for government purposes unconnected with commercial enterprise.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(b), transport vehicles used solely for which purpose are exempt from permits?

options.A: Carrying construction material for builders
options.B: Police, fire brigade, or ambulance purposes
options.C: Inter-state tourist excursions

explanation: Section 66(3)(b) exempts vehicles used for police, fire brigade, or ambulance purposes.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(i), goods carriages having gross vehicle weight not exceeding what limit can be exempted from permits by the Central Government?
explanation: Section 66(3)(i) provides exemption for any goods carriage having GVW not exceeding 3,000 kg (as notified/prescribed).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under notifications issued pursuant to Section 66, which clean-fuel transport vehicles were granted exemption from permit requirements to promote green mobility?

options.A: Pure petrol vehicles with catalytic converters
options.B: Vehicles powered by battery electric, ethanol, or methanol
options.C: Diesel vehicles with BS-VI engines

explanation: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways exempted battery electric, ethanol, and methanol powered transport vehicles from permit requirements under Section 66.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the penalty for using a vehicle without a valid permit under Section 192A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

options.A: Fine of Rs 100
options.B: Warning memo only
options.C: Imprisonment up to 6 months and/or fine up to Rs 10,000 (minimum Rs 10,000 fine for first offence)

explanation: Section 192A prescribes imprisonment up to 6 months and fine of Rs 10,000 (minimum Rs 10,000) for driving without permit.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(n), transport vehicles used for which emergency purpose are exempt from permit requirements?

options.A: Demonstration rallies
options.B: Wedding party transport during festive season
options.C: Cinema shooting crews
options.D: Carriage of relief supplies during floods, earthquake, or other natural calamity

explanation: Section 66(3)(n) exempts vehicles used for carriage of relief goods during natural disasters and civil emergencies.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a private car owner use their personal vehicle to carry fare-paying passengers on commercial routes without a permit?

options.A: Yes, if fare is reasonable
options.B: No, it violates Section 66(1) and is punishable under Section 192A
options.C: Yes, if driver holds a commercial licence

explanation: Using a private vehicle as a transport vehicle without permit directly contravenes Section 66(1) and attracts Section 192A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(c), transport vehicles used by local authorities for which purpose are exempt from permits?

options.A: Public transit bus operations
options.B: Removal of sewage or night soil and garbage
options.C: Commercial advertising hoardings

explanation: Section 66(3)(c) exempts local authority vehicles used for sewage, garbage, and public cleansing.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(2), the holder of a goods carriage permit may use the vehicle for drawing:

options.A: An unauthorized heavy machinery trailer
options.B: Any empty trailer or semi-trailer not exceeding prescribed weight
options.C: Up to 3 passenger buses

explanation: Section 66(2) allows drawing of trailers in accordance with conditions attached to goods carriage permits.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(k), vehicles used for towing disabled vehicles are:

options.A: Required to obtain national tourist permit
options.B: Exempted from permit requirements under Section 66
options.C: Required to obtain stage carriage permit

explanation: Section 66(3)(k) exempts breakdown/recovery vehicles used for towing disabled vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(p), transport vehicles used for which agricultural purpose may be exempted?

options.A: Operating commercial mobile grocery vans
options.B: Carriage of processed food to export ports
options.C: Inter-state wheat trade by wholesale dealers
options.D: Carriage of agricultural produce to marketing societies directly by the agriculturist

explanation: Transport of agricultural produce by agriculturists is granted exemptions under Section 66(3)(p).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66, which statutory authority is primarily responsible for granting transport permits in a region?

options.A: Municipal Corporation Secretary
options.B: District Police Superintendent
options.C: Public Works Department

explanation: Under Chapter V, the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) is the authority for granting permits.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a transport vehicle with a valid permit deviate from its authorized route during a road blockade?

options.A: Only if approved by the Governor
options.B: No, deviation is strictly illegal under all circumstances
options.C: Yes, but the permit is permanently cancelled immediately
options.D: Yes, if temporary detour is directed by police/competent authority due to emergency or road closure

explanation: Emergency detours directed by traffic authorities due to obstructions do not constitute illegal permit violations.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(d), transport vehicles used for which ceremonial purpose are exempt?

options.A: Wedding processions
options.B: Funeral processions and carrying corpses
options.C: Election campaign rallies

explanation: Vehicles used for funeral purposes (hearses/carrying corpses) are exempt under Section 66(3)(d).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the nature of an offence committed under Section 66(1) read with Section 192A?

options.A: Compoundable at the spot by any AMVI without limits
options.B: Cognizable offence allowing detention of vehicle under Section 207
options.C: Civil breach actionable only in consumer court

explanation: Operating without permit is a severe offence for which the vehicle can be detained under Section 207.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66, what permit is required by a stage carriage bus operating between two fixed towns on scheduled timetable?

options.A: Goods carriage permit
options.B: Contract carriage permit
options.C: Private service permit

explanation: A bus carrying passengers at separate fares on scheduled routes requires a stage carriage permit.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66, what permit is granted to a tourist bus hired as a whole under an express contract?

options.A: Stage carriage permit
options.B: Contract carriage permit
options.C: National goods permit

explanation: A bus engaged as a whole on contract basis operates under a contract carriage permit.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 66(3)(f), vehicles used for testing or trial purposes by manufacturers or body builders are:

options.A: Allowed only on race tracks
options.B: Required to take full 5-year stage carriage permit
options.C: Treated as unregistered illegal vehicles
options.D: Exempted from permit requirements subject to prescribed conditions

explanation: Vehicles under test/trial by manufacturers or coach builders are exempt under Section 66(3)(f).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 99(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, who is empowered to formulate and publish a proposal regarding road transport service of a State Transport Undertaking (STU)?

options.A: The Union Ministry of Road Transport
options.B: The District Collector
options.C: The Transport Commissioner alone

explanation: Under Section 99(1), the State Government is empowered to formulate and publish proposals/schemes for STUs.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory objective stated in Section 99 for formulating a scheme for a State Transport Undertaking?

options.A: To maximize commercial revenue for local municipal bodies
options.B: Providing an efficient, adequate, economical and properly coordinated road transport service in public interest
options.C: To eliminate all private commercial transport permanently
options.D: To increase diesel consumption across public depots

explanation: Section 99 states the objective: 'for the purpose of providing an efficient, adequate, economical and properly coordinated road transport service'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 99, where must the preliminary proposal regarding nationalization or STU monopoly of a route/area be published?

options.A: In the Supreme Court registry
options.B: On social media handles of KSRTC
options.C: Only on the notice board of the Secretariat
options.D: In the Official Gazette and in not less than one newspaper in regional language

explanation: Section 99(1) requires publication in the Official Gazette and in newspapers circulating in the area.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Chapter VI of the MV Act, an STU scheme under Section 99 may provide for operation to the:

options.A: Total ban on pedestrian and bicycle movements
options.B: Exclusion of military and ambulance vehicles only
options.C: Exclusive benefit of political parties
options.D: Complete exclusion of private operators, or partial exclusion, or in coordination with other operators

explanation: Section 99 allows a scheme to provide for operation to the exclusion, complete or partial, of other persons or otherwise.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Who has the right to file objections against a preliminary STU proposal published under Section 99?

options.A: Only the Chairman of the STU
options.B: Any person affected by the proposal under Section 100
options.C: Only registered automobile manufacturers

explanation: Under Section 100(1), any person affected by the proposal published under Section 99 may file objections.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Within how many days from publication must objections to a Section 99 proposal be filed under Section 100(1)?

options.A: Within 15 days
options.B: Within 60 days
options.C: Within 30 days

explanation: Section 100(1) prescribes 30 days from publication for filing objections to the scheme.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What happens to existing private stage carriage permits operating on a route once an approved STU monopoly scheme under Chapter VI is finalized?

options.A: They continue forever with full protection
options.B: Private permits on the notified route are cancelled, curtailed, or modified under Section 102/103 to give effect to the scheme
options.C: Private operators take over the STU depots
options.D: Private permits are automatically upgraded to air-conditioned national permits

explanation: Under Section 102/103, existing private permits are cancelled or curtailed to give effect to an approved scheme.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: In Kerala, which entity is the 'State Transport Undertaking' (STU) operating under Chapter VI of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

options.A: Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) Kerala
options.B: Kerala State Industrial Development Corporation (KSIDC)
options.C: Kerala Automobiles Limited (KAL)

explanation: KSRTC is the statutory State Transport Undertaking established under the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950 operating under Chapter VI.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 99, can a State Government modify or cancel an existing approved STU scheme?

options.A: No, an approved scheme is permanent and irreversible
options.B: Yes, the State Government may at any time formulate a proposal to modify or cancel the scheme following prescribed procedure
options.C: Only if directed by the United Nations

explanation: Under Section 102, the State Government may at any time cancel or modify any approved scheme following procedure.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Chapter VI, does the provisions of an approved STU scheme override the general provisions of Chapter V (Permits)?

options.A: No, Chapter V always overrides Chapter VI
options.B: Yes, the provisions of Chapter VI and schemes approved thereunder have overriding effect over Chapter V (Section 98)
options.C: Both chapters have equal weight and cancel each other out

explanation: Section 98 explicitly declares that Chapter VI and rules/orders made thereunder shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in Chapter V.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, every motor vehicle shall be so constructed and maintained as to be at all times:

options.A: Equipped with four-wheel drive technology
options.B: Under the effective control of the person driving the vehicle
options.C: Capable of achieving minimum 100 km/h speed

explanation: Section 109(1) stipulates that every motor vehicle shall be so constructed and maintained as to be at all times under the effective control of the person driving the vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 109(3) introduced by the 2019 Amendment empowers the Central Government to mandate the installation of which electronic safety equipment in specified motor vehicles?

options.A: Subwoofers with active bass enhancement
options.B: Radar jamming countermeasures
options.C: Neon underglow decorative lamps
options.D: Vehicle location tracking devices and emergency call buttons (AIS 140)

explanation: Section 109(3) enables the Central Government to require motor vehicles or classes of vehicles to be fitted with vehicle tracking systems and panic buttons.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the Central Government may direct a manufacturer to recall motor vehicles of a particular type if:

options.A: The sales volume of the model falls below 1,000 units in a financial year
options.B: A defect in that type of motor vehicle may cause harm to the environment or to the driver or occupants of such vehicle or to other road users
options.C: The model is more than 5 years old in the market
options.D: The vehicle uses an imported electronic control unit

explanation: Section 110A(1) provides that the Central Government may direct recall if a defect in a type of motor vehicle may cause harm to the environment or occupants or other road users.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A(2), a defect in a motor vehicle may be brought to the notice of the Central Government by:

options.A: Exclusively by registered trade unions
options.B: Only by a foreign government testing authority
options.C: Only through a petition in the Supreme Court
options.D: A report from a testing agency, or an investigation by the Central Government, or complaints by not less than a prescribed percentage of purchasers

explanation: Section 110A(2) states that recall may be triggered by report of a testing agency, central investigation, or complaints from a prescribed percentage of owners.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: When a recall is ordered under Section 110A, what is the statutory duty of the manufacturer under Section 110A(3)?

options.A: To cease all vehicle manufacturing for 10 years
options.B: To publish apologies on national television only
options.C: To reimburse the purchasers the full cost of the vehicle or replace the defective vehicle or defective part without charge

explanation: Under Section 110A(3), the manufacturer must reimburse the purchasers the full cost of the vehicle or replace the defective vehicle/parts with non-defective ones.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A(5), if a manufacturer notices a defect and initiates a voluntary recall before an order is issued by the Central Government:

options.A: The manufacturer is banned from exporting vehicles
options.B: The manufacturer must pay double the statutory fine
options.C: All vehicle factories of that manufacturer will be sealed
options.D: No fine or penalty shall be imposed on the manufacturer under this section

explanation: Section 110A(5) encourages voluntary safety recalls by exempting the manufacturer from fine/penalty if voluntary recall is initiated before a government order.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum penalty leviable on a vehicle manufacturer under Section 182A(3) for failure to comply with a recall order under Section 110A?

options.A: Fine up to Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Fine up to Rs 1 crore
options.C: Fine up to Rs 500 crore

explanation: Section 182A(3) prescribes a fine which may extend to one hundred crore rupees (Rs 100 crore) for failure to comply with recall orders or supplying non-compliant vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 deals with 'Type-approval certificate and testing agencies'?

options.A: Section 112
options.B: Section 109
options.C: Section 110A

explanation: Section 110B, inserted by the 2019 Amendment, specifically governs 'Type-approval certificate and testing agencies'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110B(1), who is authorized to issue type-approval certificates to vehicle and component manufacturers?

options.A: Any private testing workshop
options.B: The testing agencies authorized and accredited by the Central Government
options.C: The local municipal health officer

explanation: Section 110B(1) provides that testing agencies authorized by the Central Government (e.g. ARAI, ICAT, CIRT, VRDE) issue type-approval certificates.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which of the following premier automotive testing and research institutions in India acts as an authorized type-approval agency under CMV Rules?

options.A: Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Pune
options.B: International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT), Manesar
options.C: Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), Pune

explanation: ARAI, ICAT, CIRT, VRDE, and CFMTTI are all authorized testing agencies accredited under CMV Rule 126 and Section 110B.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110B(2), what can happen if an authorized testing agency issues a false or misleading type-approval certificate?

options.A: Nothing, as testing agencies enjoy absolute sovereign immunity
options.B: The testing agency is given a monetary award
options.C: The testing agency is transferred to the State Police
options.D: The Central Government may withdraw its authorization and cancel its accreditation

explanation: Section 110B(2) empowers the Central Government to suspend or cancel the authorization of testing agencies issuing false/improper type-approval certificates.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109(2), the Central Government may make rules requiring the installation of which device to monitor heavy commercial vehicle operations?

options.A: Electronic speed governors
options.B: Tachographs or vehicle tracking and monitoring systems
options.C: Alcohol interlock ignition systems

explanation: Section 109 empowers the Central Government to prescribe rules for electronic monitoring, speed governors, tachographs, and safety components.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the Automotive Industry Standard (AIS) number in India governing Intelligent Transportation Systems and Vehicle Tracking Devices under Section 109?

options.A: AIS 037
options.B: AIS 004
options.C: AIS 025

explanation: AIS 140 is the standard for Vehicle Tracking Systems (VTS) and panic buttons mandated for commercial transport vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A, what standard must recalled vehicles be restored to by the manufacturer?

options.A: To the minimum scrap metal standard
options.B: To conform to the standards and specifications in force at the time of manufacture
options.C: To the latest BS-VI Stage II norms irrespective of manufacture year

explanation: Under Section 110A, the vehicle must be restored to conform to the specifications and standards that applied at the time of its original manufacture.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110B, what is the primary purpose of a Type-Approval Certificate?

options.A: To register the driver's biometric data
options.B: To certify that a prototype vehicle or component meets all prescribed safety, roadworthiness, and environmental standards before mass production
options.C: To assess the market resale value after 10 years
options.D: To grant exemption from paying road tax

explanation: Type approval certifies that a prototype complies with statutory construction, emission, and safety regulations prior to commercial sale.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109, what is the mandatory requirement for tyres used on motor vehicles under CMV Rules?

options.A: They must be retreaded at least 5 times
options.B: They must conform to BIS standards and display ISI marking
options.C: They must be imported from European Union
options.D: They must have zero tread depth for maximum contact area

explanation: CMV Rules pursuant to Section 109 mandate that pneumatic tyres must conform to BIS specifications and carry ISI mark.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A, can the Central Government initiate recall proceedings based on an electronic defect portal created for consumer complaints?

options.A: Only if the vehicle caught fire in Parliament premises
options.B: No, consumer complaints have no legal validity
options.C: Only if each complainant files a civil suit in Delhi
options.D: Yes, public complaints on the designated government portal can trigger an investigation and recall

explanation: Under Section 110A and the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, an online portal (Vahan / MoRTH recall portal) aggregates consumer complaints to evaluate recall triggers.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which testing agency under Section 110B functions under the Ministry of Defence and conducts testing of military and civil vehicles at Ahmednagar?

options.A: Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI)
options.B: Indian Institute of Petroleum (IIP)
options.C: Global Automotive Research Centre (GARC)

explanation: VRDE Ahmednagar is a DRDO laboratory accredited as an authorized testing agency under CMV Rule 126.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109, who has the power to specify the standards for construction, equipment, and maintenance of motor vehicles in India?

options.A: Local village councils
options.B: The State Government exclusively
options.C: Individual vehicle dealers

explanation: Section 109 and Section 110 give overriding rule-making powers regarding vehicle construction, equipment, and safety standards to the Central Government.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A, if a manufacturer replaces a recalled defective vehicle, the warranty on the replacement vehicle shall:

options.A: Be completely voided
options.B: Commence afresh as for a new vehicle
options.C: Be limited to 3 days

explanation: Under Section 110A and recall rules, when a vehicle is replaced, normal new vehicle warranty and protections apply.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under CMV Rules framed pursuant to Section 109, what is the maximum permissible speed preset in a Speed Limiting Device (Speed Governor) for standard dumpers/school buses?

options.A: 150 km/h for heavy multi-axle trucks
options.B: 120 km/h across all vehicles
options.C: 80 km/h for all passenger cars
options.D: School buses: 40 km/h; Dumpers: 60 km/h (or 50/40 km/h as notified by State Governments)

explanation: CMV Rules prescribe preset maximum speed limits for speed governors (e.g., 40/50 km/h for school buses and hazardous tankers, 80 km/h for commercial transport vehicles).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110B, what is Conformity of Production (COP)?

options.A: An annual audit of showroom sales staff
options.B: A ceremony where new car buyers meet the design engineers
options.C: An agreement between all car manufacturers to fix car prices
options.D: A procedure ensuring that mass-produced vehicles and components continuously match the approved prototype specifications

explanation: COP (Conformity of Production) is the periodic testing procedure ensuring vehicles manufactured on the assembly line match the type-approved prototype.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109, retro-reflective tapes on commercial transport vehicles must conform to which color standard under CMV Rules?

options.A: Yellow on front, Green on sides, Blue on rear
options.B: White on front, Yellow on sides, and Red on rear
options.C: Black on front, Purple on sides, Pink on rear
options.D: Red on front, White on sides, Yellow on rear

explanation: Under CMV Rule 104, commercial vehicles must carry retro-reflective contour markings: White on front, Yellow on both sides, and Red at the rear.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A, the report of an investigation for vehicle recall is prepared by:

options.A: A private taxi drivers guild
options.B: A local car dealership union
options.C: The insurance ombudsman
options.D: An officer or committee designated by the Central Government

explanation: Under Section 110A(2), an investigation is conducted by an officer or independent body authorized by the Central Government.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109, what is the mandatory requirement for rear-under-run protection devices (RUPD) and lateral under-run protection devices (LUPD) on heavy goods vehicles?

options.A: To provide a cosmetic look to the truck
options.B: To prevent smaller passenger vehicles and two-wheelers from sliding under the chassis during a collision
options.C: To carry extra diesel cans

explanation: RUPD and LUPD are mandatory safety barriers under AIS / CMV Rules to prevent underrunning of smaller vehicles during impacts.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110B, which testing agency is located in Chennai under the NATRiP project?

options.A: CIRT
options.B: ICAT
options.C: ARAI

explanation: GARC (Global Automotive Research Centre) is located at Oragadam near Chennai, established under NATRiP.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109, the fitment of an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) has been made mandatory for:

options.A: Only hand-pulled rickshaws
options.B: Only Formula 1 racing cars
options.C: Only agricultural tractors operating in paddy fields
options.D: All two-wheelers above 125cc and all M and N category commercial vehicles

explanation: ABS is statutorily mandatory for all commercial vehicles (M2, M3, N2, N3) and two-wheelers exceeding 125 cc engine capacity.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110A, failure of a manufacturer to issue a recall notice when directed by the Central Government can result in:

options.A: No consequence because recall is purely optional
options.B: Permanent transfer of factory ownership to the RTO
options.C: Suspension of the driver's driving licence
options.D: Cancellation of type-approval certification and heavy fiscal fines under Section 182A(3)

explanation: Non-compliance with recall directives under Section 110A leads to massive fines up to Rs 100 crore and revocation of type approval.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 109, what standard regulates child restraint systems (child car seats) fitted in passenger cars?

options.A: BS-IV
options.B: AIS 001

explanation: Child restraint systems are regulated under AIS 072 conforming to UN ECE regulations.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 110B, what is the validity period of a Type-Approval Certificate for a vehicle model?

options.A: It expires every December 31 regardless of standards
options.B: Strictly 30 days from prototype build
options.C: Exactly 6 months
options.D: It remains valid as long as the vehicle model continues in production conforming to applicable COP norms and unchanged regulatory standards

explanation: Type approval remains valid until applicable regulatory norms change or manufacturer modifies specifications requiring extension of type approval.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 112(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, no person shall drive a motor vehicle:

options.A: Without headlights on in broad daylight
options.B: At a speed exceeding the maximum speed or below the minimum speed fixed for the vehicle or for any specified area
options.C: Without playing FM radio
options.D: Unless accompanied by at least two passengers

explanation: Section 112(1) prohibits driving at a speed exceeding the maximum speed or below the minimum speed fixed for the vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Who is empowered under Section 112(1) to fix maximum and minimum speed limits on roads across India?

options.A: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority
options.B: Private toll concessionaires arbitrarily
options.C: Automobile manufacturers
options.D: The Central Government, or State Government / local authority within their respective jurisdictions

explanation: Section 112 empowers Central Government (especially for national highways) and State Governments / local authorities to fix speed limits.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the MoRTH speed limit notification for Expressways, what is the maximum speed limit for M1 category passenger cars (up to 8 seats)?

options.A: 100 km/h
options.B: 120 km/h
options.C: 140 km/h

explanation: The maximum speed limit on Expressways for M1 category cars is 120 km/h (100 km/h on 4-lane national highways).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum speed limit for goods vehicles (Category N) on National Highways with 4 or more lanes?

options.A: 60 km/h
options.B: 70 km/h
options.C: 80 km/h

explanation: The national speed limit for goods carriages (Category N) on 4-lane divided National Highways is 80 km/h.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 113(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, no person shall drive any motor vehicle or trailer:

options.A: Without carrying a valid credit card
options.B: The unladen weight of which exceeds the unladen weight specified in the certificate of registration
options.C: Which has less than 2 spare tyres
options.D: Whose battery is made of lead-acid

explanation: Section 113(1) prohibits driving any vehicle the unladen weight of which exceeds the unladen weight specified in the RC.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 113(2), driving a motor vehicle whose gross vehicle weight or axle weight exceeds the maximum permissible limit is:

options.A: Allowed during nighttime between 10 PM and 5 AM
options.B: Permitted on payment of extra toll at toll gates
options.C: Permitted if the driver signs a declaration

explanation: Section 113(2) strictly bars driving any vehicle where GVW or any axle weight exceeds certified limits.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 114(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, an authorized officer of the Motor Vehicles Department may require the driver to drive the vehicle to a weighbridge within what distance?

options.A: Not more than 5 km from the point of interception
options.B: Not more than 10 km from the direction of travel
options.C: Not more than 20 km
options.D: Any distance across the entire state

explanation: Section 114(1) authorizes officers to direct the driver to take the vehicle to a weighbridge lying within a distance of not more than 10 km from the direction of travel.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 114(2), if an officer detects overloading upon weighing, what MUST the driver do before being allowed to move the vehicle further?

options.A: Pay a bribe to the weighbridge operator
options.B: Offload the excess weight at his own risk and cost until the vehicle complies with permissible weight limits
options.C: Drive faster to reach destination quickly
options.D: Deflate the tyres to reduce ground pressure

explanation: Section 114(2) mandates that the driver shall offload excess weight at his own risk and expense before proceeding.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Who is responsible for the custody, risk, and expense of goods offloaded under Section 114(2)?

options.A: The inspecting AMVI personally
options.B: The driver and owner of the motor vehicle
options.C: The State Government treasury

explanation: Under Section 114(2), offloading is strictly at the risk and expense of the driver/owner.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 120 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, no person shall drive a motor vehicle with left-hand steering control unless:

options.A: It is painted yellow
options.B: It is equipped with a mechanical or electrical signalling device of a prescribed nature
options.C: It carries two steering wheels
options.D: It is driven only in reverse gear

explanation: Section 120 mandates that vehicles with left-hand steering control must be equipped with prescribed mechanical or electrical signalling devices.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 122 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, leaving a motor vehicle in a dangerous position means leaving it:

options.A: Inside an authorized paid parking lot
options.B: In a public place in a position or condition or circumstance as to cause or be likely to cause danger, obstruction, or undue inconvenience to other road users
options.C: With headlights switched off in a private driveway
options.D: In front of one's own residential garage

explanation: Section 122 prohibits abandoning or leaving a vehicle in any public place so as to cause danger, obstruction, or undue inconvenience.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 123(1) of the MV Act, 1988, riding on which part of a motor vehicle is strictly prohibited?

options.A: On the authorized pillion seat behind the driver
options.B: On the front passenger seat with seat belt fastened
options.C: In the rear row of a maxi cab
options.D: On the running board, top, or bonnet of the vehicle

explanation: Section 123(1) prohibits riding on the running board, top roof, or bonnet of any motor vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 123(2), what is the liability of the driver if persons ride on the running board or roof of a stage carriage bus?

options.A: The driver is exempted if passengers bought tickets
options.B: No person driving or in charge shall permit any person to ride on the running board, top, or bonnet; driver is liable under Section 123 and penal sections
options.C: The conductor alone is liable, driver has zero liability
options.D: Passengers ride at their own risk with no driver liability

explanation: Section 123(2) prohibits the driver or person in charge from permitting any person to ride on running boards, top, or bonnet.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 125(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, no person driving a motor vehicle shall allow any person to stand or sit, or anything to be placed, in such a manner or position as to:

options.A: Increase fuel consumption
options.B: Hamper the driver in his control of the vehicle
options.C: Block the view of rear seat passengers

explanation: Section 125(1) forbids allowing any person or object to hamper the driver in the control of the vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 125(2) inserted by the 2019 Amendment, which act is specifically prohibited while driving a motor vehicle?

options.A: Glancing at the speedometer
options.B: Looking into the side rear-view mirror
options.C: Operating the air conditioning temperature knob
options.D: Using a hand-held mobile phone or other communication device while driving (except navigation assistance in prescribed manner)

explanation: Section 125(2) prohibits using mobile communication devices while driving, except for navigational purposes used hands-free.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 126 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what precaution MUST a driver take before leaving a vehicle stationary in any public place?

options.A: Leave the engine running on idle with hazard lights on
options.B: Stop the mechanism and apply the brakes or take other measures to prevent the vehicle from moving in his absence
options.C: Hand over the keys to any passerby
options.D: Leave the vehicle in neutral on a slope without handbrake

explanation: Section 126 mandates stopping the engine mechanism and applying brakes to ensure the vehicle cannot move in the driver's absence.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 127(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, who is empowered to remove a vehicle abandoned or left unattended in a public place for 10 hours or more?

options.A: Any passing pedestrian
options.B: Any police officer having jurisdiction or authorized officer of the Motor Vehicles Department
options.C: Only the nearest scrap dealer

explanation: Section 127(1) empowers police officers and authorized MVD officers to tow away or remove abandoned/unattended vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 127(2), who is liable to pay the towing and storage charges for an abandoned vehicle removed by authorities?

options.A: The general taxpayers
options.B: The owner of the vehicle
options.C: The recovery vehicle driver

explanation: Section 127(2) provides that towing charges and custody/storage charges shall be recovered from the owner of the vehicle.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 128(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, how many persons in addition to the driver can legally ride on a two-wheeled motorcycle?

options.A: Two persons
options.B: No more than one person
options.C: Three persons if one is a child
options.D: Up to four persons in rural areas

explanation: Section 128(1) strictly limits two-wheeler carriage to not more than one person in addition to the driver (i.e. maximum 2 riders total).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 128(1), how must a pillion passenger sit on a two-wheeled motorcycle?

options.A: Standing behind the driver
options.B: Sitting sideways without footrests
options.C: Sitting on a proper seat securely fixed to the motorcycle behind the driver's seat
options.D: Sitting on the petrol tank in front of driver

explanation: Section 128(1) mandates sitting on a proper seat securely fixed to the motorcycle behind the driver.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the Central Motor Vehicles (Second Amendment) Rules, 2022 (Rule 138(7) pursuant to Section 128/129), what safety gear is mandatory for children between 9 months and 4 years riding as pillion on a motorcycle?

options.A: Reflective high-visibility jacket alone
options.B: Only woollen gloves
options.C: Only safety goggles
options.D: A safety harness connecting the child to the rider and a crash helmet / bicycle helmet conforming to standards

explanation: Rule 138(7) requires a safety harness attaching the child to the driver, a crash helmet, and caps the motorcycle speed at 40 km/h.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum speed permitted for a motorcycle carrying a child up to 4 years old as per Central Motor Vehicles Rules?

options.A: 20 km/h
options.B: 30 km/h
options.C: 40 km/h

explanation: Under CMV Rule 138(7), the speed of the motorcycle carrying a child up to 4 years shall not exceed 40 km/h.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 129 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), who MUST wear protective headgear while driving or riding on a motorcycle in a public place?

options.A: Only male drivers above 18 years
options.B: Every person, above four years of age, driving or riding on a motorcycle of any class or description
options.C: Only the driver, pillion riders are exempt
options.D: Only riders traveling on National Highways

explanation: Section 129 mandates that every person above 4 years of age driving or riding on a motorcycle shall wear protective headgear.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 129, what specification must the protective headgear (helmet) conform to?

options.A: Any plastic cap
options.B: Standards specified by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS - IS 4151)
options.C: Industrial construction hard hat

explanation: Section 129 mandates helmets conforming to the standards of the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which community is EXEMPT from wearing protective headgear under the proviso to Section 129?

options.A: Government employees in uniform
options.B: College students below 21 years
options.C: Persons driving within 2 km of their home
options.D: A Sikh person wearing a turban while driving or riding a motorcycle

explanation: The proviso to Section 129 exempts any person who is a Sikh wearing a turban.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 131 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what is the duty of the driver of a motor vehicle approaching an unguarded railway level crossing?

options.A: Speed up to cross the tracks before any train arrives
options.B: Stop the vehicle, ensure no train is approaching from either side, and in case of a transport vehicle, cause the conductor or an attendant to walk up to the track before crossing
options.C: Blow the horn continuously and cross without stopping
options.D: Switch off headlights and proceed slowly

explanation: Section 131 mandates stopping, checking for trains, and for transport vehicles, having the conductor/driver walk up to the track to ensure safe clearance.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 132(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a driver MUST stop the motor vehicle in which of the following circumstances?

options.A: When required to do so by any police officer in uniform not below the rank of a police constable
options.B: When required by an authorized officer of the Motor Vehicles Department
options.C: When the vehicle is involved in the occurrence of an accident to a person, animal, or another vehicle

explanation: Section 132(1) mandates stopping when directed by police in uniform, MVD officers, or upon involvement in an accident.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what is the duty of the owner of a motor vehicle when demanded by a police officer or MVD officer?

options.A: To surrender the vehicle immediately
options.B: To give all information regarding the name and address of, and the licence held by, the driver who drove the vehicle at any relevant time
options.C: To pay all traffic challans across the entire district
options.D: To purchase new tyres for the vehicle

explanation: Section 133 requires the owner to furnish the name, address, and licence details of the driver driving at the time of an offence or accident.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 134(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what is the primary duty of the driver when a person is injured in a motor vehicle accident?

options.A: Flee the scene immediately to avoid police questioning
options.B: Take all reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person, and convey him to the nearest hospital or medical practitioner
options.C: Negotiate a private financial settlement with onlookers
options.D: Hide the vehicle in a distant garage

explanation: Section 134(a) mandates securing medical attention and conveying the injured to the nearest doctor/hospital immediately.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the proviso to Section 134(a), a driver is excused from conveying an injured person to hospital ONLY if:

options.A: The driver does not have sufficient cash
options.B: It is not practicable to do so on account of mob fury or any other reason beyond his control
options.C: The hospital is more than 3 km away

explanation: The proviso excuses the driver from immediate personal conveyance only if mob fury or circumstances beyond control prevent it.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 134(b), within what time must the driver report the details of an accident involving injury to a person to the nearest police station?

options.A: Within 1 hour
options.B: Within 24 hours (as soon as possible and in any case within twenty-four hours)
options.C: Within 7 days

explanation: Section 134(b) requires reporting to the nearest police station as soon as possible and in any case within 24 hours.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 134(c) introduced by the 2019 Amendment, the driver or owner must furnish accident information to which entity?

options.A: The nearest petrol pump manager
options.B: The vehicle loan financing bank
options.C: The local newspaper editor
options.D: The designated insurer of the motor vehicle

explanation: Section 134(c) requires furnishing information to the insurance company that issued the policy.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 134A inserted by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides for:

options.A: Mandatory blood alcohol testing of all drivers
options.B: Protection of Good Samaritans who assist accident victims
options.C: Immediate auction of accident vehicles

explanation: Section 134A provides comprehensive protection to Good Samaritans from civil or criminal liability and harassment.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 134A(1), a Good Samaritan who voluntarily provides medical or non-medical assistance to an accident victim is:

options.A: Subject to mandatory police detention for 48 hours
options.B: Compelled to pay the initial hospital admission charges
options.C: Not liable for any civil or criminal action for any injury to or death of the victim of an accident resulting from his assistance
options.D: Required to act as the chief prosecution witness in court

explanation: Section 134A(1) protects Good Samaritans from any civil or criminal liability resulting from assistance rendered in good faith.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 134A(2), can a police officer or hospital authority force a Good Samaritan to disclose their identity or personal details?
