question: Under the proviso to Section 146(1), which vehicles may be exempted from compulsory third-party insurance by the appropriate Government?

options.A: Commercial taxis operating under aggregators
options.B: All luxury private imported sports cars
options.C: All two-wheelers below 150 cc
options.D: Any motor vehicle owned by the Central Government or a State Government and used for government purposes unconnected with commercial enterprise

explanation: Vehicles owned by Central/State governments used for non-commercial purposes can be exempted if a dedicated insurance fund is established.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146(2), a local authority or State transport undertaking can be exempted from third-party insurance if:

options.A: It declares itself bankrupt
options.B: It establishes and maintains an approved fund for meeting third-party liabilities in accordance with prescribed rules
options.C: It pays an annual fee to the High Court
options.D: It operates only within 10 km of the depot

explanation: Section 146(2) allows exemption for local authorities/STUs that maintain an approved third-party liability insurance fund.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory penalty for driving an uninsured motor vehicle under Section 196 of the MV Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019)?

options.A: Fine of Rs 100 only
options.B: First offence: imprisonment up to 3 months and/or fine of Rs 2,000; Second offence: imprisonment up to 3 months and/or fine of Rs 4,000
options.C: Compulsory life imprisonment
options.D: A simple verbal warning from the traffic constable

explanation: Section 196 prescribes imprisonment up to 3 months and/or fine of Rs 2,000 for 1st offence, and up to Rs 4,000 / 3 months for subsequent offences.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146, does a Comprehensive Insurance Policy (Package Policy) satisfy the legal requirement of the Act?

options.A: No, comprehensive policies are illegal in India
options.B: Yes, because a comprehensive policy contains Section II covering mandatory Third-Party Liability in compliance with Chapter XI
options.C: Only if endorsed by the Transport Commissioner
options.D: Only if the vehicle is brand new

explanation: A comprehensive policy covers both Own Damage (OD) and the statutory Third Party (TP) liability required under Section 146.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the Supreme Court mandate implemented in 2018, what is the mandatory minimum upfront third-party insurance tenure for a brand-new two-wheeler at registration?

options.A: 1 year
options.B: 3 years
options.C: 5 years

explanation: The Supreme Court mandated a 5-year upfront third-party insurance policy for new two-wheelers and 3-year upfront policy for new private cars.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the mandatory upfront third-party insurance tenure for a brand-new private four-wheeler (car) at the time of purchase?

options.A: 1 year
options.B: 2 years
options.C: 3 years

explanation: A 3-year upfront third-party insurance policy is mandatory for new private four-wheelers.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Chapter XI of the MV Act, who is considered a 'third party'?

options.A: The vehicle owner (first party)
options.B: The insurance company (second party)
options.C: Any person other than the insurer and the insured (such as pedestrians, passengers, or occupants of other vehicles)

explanation: The insured is the 1st party, the insurer is the 2nd party, and any other person suffering loss/injury is the 3rd party.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, what is the statutory limit on an insurer's liability for third-party death or bodily injury in a motor accident?

options.A: Limited to Rs 50,000
options.B: Limited to Rs 5 lakh
options.C: Unlimited (the insurer must indemnify the full amount of compensation awarded by the MACT)
options.D: Limited to the depreciated value of the vehicle

explanation: Under Section 147, the liability of the insurer for death or bodily injury of a third party is unlimited.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 147(2), what is the statutory limit of third-party property damage (TPPD) liability covered by an insurer unless a higher premium is paid?
explanation: Under Section 147(2), the standard limit for damage to property of a third party is Rs 7,50,000 (seven lakh fifty thousand rupees).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Does Section 146 apply when a motor vehicle is driven inside a public park, bus stand, or market road?

options.A: No, it applies only on National Highways
options.B: Yes, the definition of 'public place' under Section 2(34) covers any road, street, way, or other place to which the public have a right of access
options.C: Only if toll is paid
options.D: Only if traffic police are on duty

explanation: Section 146 applies to all 'public places', defined broadly in Section 2(34) as any place to which the public have access.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146, what document serves as conclusive proof that a motor vehicle is insured in compliance with Chapter XI?

options.A: The original sales invoice from car dealer
options.B: A valid Certificate of Insurance issued by the insurer in prescribed Form
options.C: The driver's PAN card
options.D: A bank passbook showing premium deduction

explanation: Under Section 147(3) and CMV Rules, a Certificate of Insurance is the statutory proof of valid insurance.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an insurer avoid third-party liability towards a crash victim on the ground that the driver was driving without a valid driving licence?

options.A: Yes, the victim gets nothing
options.B: The insurer must pay the compensation to the third-party victim first and may subsequently recover the sum from the vehicle owner (Pay and Recover principle)
options.C: The victim must sue the RTO officer

explanation: Under established Supreme Court jurisprudence (Swaran Singh case), the insurer must pay the third party and recover from the insured.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146, is a trailer attached to a tractor or prime mover required to be covered by third-party insurance?

options.A: No, trailers are not motor vehicles
options.B: Yes, trailers and semi-trailers must also be covered by insurance when used in a public place
options.C: Only if the trailer carries hazardous chemicals
options.D: Only if the trailer is painted blue

explanation: Trailers drawn by motor vehicles must also be covered for third-party risk while in use on public roads.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the consequence if a vehicle owner allows their third-party insurance to lapse even for a single day while the vehicle is kept on a public road?

options.A: The vehicle has 90 days automatic immunity
options.B: Using or keeping the vehicle in a public place violates Section 146 and is punishable under Section 196
options.C: The vehicle registration is permanently cancelled

explanation: Section 146 requires continuous insurance; keeping or using an uninsured vehicle on a public road attracts Section 196.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146, does compulsory third-party insurance cover injury to a gratuitous passenger traveling in a goods carriage truck?

options.A: Yes, all persons anywhere in a vehicle are fully covered
options.B: No, gratuitous passengers carried in a goods carriage are not covered by statutory third-party policy (Asha Rani case)
options.C: Covered only if passenger holds an AMVI certificate

explanation: The Supreme Court held in New India Assurance v. Asha Rani that statutory third-party policies do not cover gratuitous passengers in goods carriages.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 149 of the MV Act (as amended in 2019), who is responsible for preparing and submitting the Detailed Accident Report (DAR) to the Claims Tribunal and Insurer within prescribed timelines?

options.A: The local MLA
options.B: The investigating Police Officer
options.C: The vehicle manufacturer

explanation: Under Section 159 and Claims Tribunal rules, the investigating police officer must submit the DAR / FAR within prescribed deadlines.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146, does compulsory third-party insurance cover the owner of the vehicle (owner-driver)?

options.A: Yes, owner is treated as third party
options.B: No, the owner is the 'First Party' and is covered under mandatory Personal Accident (CPA) cover, not as a third party
options.C: The owner has no insurance coverage under Indian law
options.D: Owner is covered only if vehicle is electric

explanation: The owner is the first party. Compulsory Personal Accident (CPA) cover of Rs 15 lakh protects the owner-driver separately.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a motor vehicle be registered or have its fitness certificate renewed by an RTO without a valid insurance certificate under Section 146?

options.A: Yes, insurance is optional during registration
options.B: No, production of a valid certificate of insurance is a mandatory statutory prerequisite for registration, renewal, and fitness certification
options.C: Only private two-wheelers can register without insurance
options.D: Insurance is checked only after an accident occurs

explanation: Under Section 146 read with CMV Rules, valid insurance is an indispensable statutory prerequisite for registration and fitness certification.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with IRDAI guidelines, does an electronic insurance policy (e-insurance) displayed via mParivahan or DigiLocker hold equal legal validity as a physical certificate of insurance?

options.A: No, only physical hard copies printed on green paper are accepted
options.B: Yes, digital insurance certificates stored and presented through government DigiLocker or mParivahan apps are legally valid and recognized by enforcement authorities
options.C: Valid only if verified at a notary public office
options.D: Valid only for two-wheelers below 100 cc

explanation: Under MoRTH notifications and IRDAI regulations, electronic documents (including driving licence, RC, and insurance) presented via DigiLocker or mParivahan are statutorily recognized under the IT Act, 2000 and Section 146.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), what is the maximum fine for a first offence where no specific penalty is provided?

options.A: Fine up to Rs 2,000
options.B: Fine up to Rs 100
options.C: Fine up to Rs 1,000

explanation: Section 177 provides that whoever contravenes any provision of the Act or rules where no specific penalty is provided shall be punishable for the first offence with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (Rs 500).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum fine for a second or subsequent offence under Section 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988?

options.A: Fine up to Rs 500
options.B: Fine up to Rs 1,000
options.C: Fine up to Rs 1,500

explanation: Under Section 177, for any second or subsequent offence, the fine may extend to one thousand five hundred rupees (Rs 1,500).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Prior to the 2019 Amendment, what were the fine amounts under Section 177 for first and second offences respectively?

options.A: Rs 50 and Rs 100
options.B: Rs 100 and Rs 300
options.C: Rs 200 and Rs 500

explanation: Prior to the 2019 amendment, Section 177 provided a fine of up to Rs 100 for the first offence and up to Rs 300 for subsequent offences.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which of the following violations is commonly penalized under Section 177 due to lack of a distinct specific penal section?

options.A: Racing on public roads without permit
options.B: Driving under the influence of alcohol (BAC > 30 mg/100 ml)
options.C: Driving without a valid driving licence
options.D: Driving without rear-view mirrors or without functional high-beam indicator

explanation: Minor equipment infractions (e.g. missing mirrors, non-functional horn, dirty number plate) have no specific penalty sections and are prosecuted under the general penalty Section 177.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a court award imprisonment for an offence prosecuted strictly under Section 177?

options.A: Yes, up to 6 months
options.B: Yes, up to 1 month
options.C: No, Section 177 prescribes only a pecuniary fine and does not provide for imprisonment
options.D: Only if the offender refuses to pay fine

explanation: Section 177 provides exclusively for monetary fines (Rs 500 / Rs 1,500) and no substantive term of imprisonment.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 177, does an offence committed two years after a previous conviction count as a 'subsequent offence'?

options.A: No, previous offences expire after 6 months
options.B: Yes, any second or subsequent commission of an offence under the section attracts enhanced penalty
options.C: Only if committed in the same police station limits
options.D: Only if committed using the exact same vehicle

explanation: A subsequent offence under Section 177 refers to repeating an offence under the Act/Rules after a prior conviction.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 177, who has the authority to compound the offence on the spot?

options.A: Any traffic warden
options.B: Officers authorized by the State Government under Section 200
options.C: Only Judicial First Class Magistrates

explanation: Section 177 is compoundable by officers authorized by the State Government under Section 200 of the MV Act.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a driver fails to display an 'L' board while driving with a learner's licence, which penal section applies?

options.A: Section 181
options.B: Section 184
options.C: Section 177 (or Section 177A)

explanation: Violation of CMV Rule 3 (L-board display) has no separate specific penal section and is charged under Section 177 / 177A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the compounding fee fixed in Kerala for a first offence under Section 177?

options.B: Rs 500
options.C: Rs 100

explanation: In Kerala, under the compounding notifications, general first offences under Section 177 are compounded at Rs 250 (or statutory maximum Rs 500).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 177 is titled as:

options.A: Punishment for abetment of offences
options.B: General provision for punishment of offences
options.C: Offences relating to driving licences

explanation: Section 177 is titled 'General provision for punishment of offences'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 177A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 prescribes penalty for contravention of regulations made under which section?

options.A: Section 112 (Speed limits)
options.B: Section 118 (Driving regulations)
options.C: Section 129 (Helmets)

explanation: Section 177A specifically penalizes contravention of the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations made under Section 118.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the penalty prescribed under Section 177A for violating the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017?

options.A: Fine of Rs 100
options.B: Fine not less than five hundred rupees, but may extend to one thousand rupees (Rs 500 to Rs 1,000)
options.C: Imprisonment for 3 months

explanation: Section 177A prescribes a fine of not less than five hundred rupees, but which may extend to one thousand rupees.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which of the following violations falls squarely under Section 177A?

options.A: Failing to produce RC under Section 44
options.B: Overloading a goods truck by 5 tonnes
options.C: Driving without insurance under Section 146
options.D: Improper lane changing without indicator under Regulation 7 of Driving Regulations, 2017

explanation: Violating driving behavior rules framed under Section 118 (e.g. improper lane changing, improper turning) is punished under Section 177A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 177A, failing to give way to traffic on your right at an uncontrolled roundabout violates which regulation?

options.A: Section 192A
options.B: Section 185
options.C: Section 181
options.D: Regulation 14 of MV (Driving) Regulations, 2017 and is punishable under Section 177A

explanation: Roundabout right-of-way rules are in Regulation 14, punishable under Section 177A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Was Section 177A present in the original 1988 Act or inserted later?

options.A: Present in the original 1988 Act
options.B: Inserted by the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019
options.C: Inserted by the 1994 Amendment

explanation: Section 177A was inserted by the 2019 Amendment to specifically enforce the Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Overtaking from the left side in violation of Regulation 6 of the MV (Driving) Regulations, 2017 is penalized under:

options.A: Section 146
options.B: Section 194
options.C: Section 196

explanation: Overtaking violations under the Driving Regulations are punishable under Section 177A (or Section 184 if dangerously executed).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Failure to observe the 'Stop' line or reversing onto a main road unlawfully is punishable under:

options.A: Section 198
options.B: Section 110A
options.C: Section 213

explanation: Reversing and road-marking contraventions under the Driving Regulations fall under Section 177A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an offence under Section 177A be compounded by authorized officers?

options.A: Only by the District Collector
options.B: No, it requires summary trial before High Court
options.C: Compounding is permitted only on national holidays
options.D: Yes, under Section 200 of the Act

explanation: Section 177A offences are compoundable under Section 200.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178(1) of the MV Act, 1988, what is the maximum fine for a passenger travelling in a stage carriage without a valid pass or ticket?

options.A: Fine up to Rs 50
options.B: Fine up to Rs 500
options.C: Fine up to Rs 1,000

explanation: Section 178(1) prescribes a fine which may extend to five hundred rupees (Rs 500) for travelling without a valid pass or ticket.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178(1), in addition to the fine, what else must the ticketless passenger pay?

options.A: Five times the annual road tax
options.B: A mandatory hotel stay voucher
options.C: Double the cost of a full bus tank of diesel
options.D: The ordinary fare for the distance which he has travelled, or from the point of departure of the vehicle if distance cannot be ascertained

explanation: Section 178(1) mandates payment of the ordinary fare from the starting point if distance is unascertainable, along with the fine.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178(2), what penalty is prescribed for a conductor who willfully neglects or refuses to supply a ticket to a passenger after collecting fare?

options.A: Imprisonment for 5 years
options.B: Fine up to Rs 50 only
options.C: Suspension of conductor's badge for 10 years

explanation: Section 178(2) punishes dereliction of duty by a conductor (failing to issue ticket, fraudulent tickets) with fine up to Rs 500.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178(3)(a), if the driver of a contract carriage (such as an auto-rickshaw or taxi cab) refuses to ply the vehicle without reasonable excuse, what is the fine?

options.A: Fine up to Rs 5,000
options.B: Fine up to Rs 500
options.C: Fine up to Rs 2,000

explanation: Under Section 178(3)(a), a contract carriage driver refusing to ply or carrying passengers contrary to conditions is punishable with fine up to Rs 50.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178(3)(b), what is the penalty if a contract carriage driver refuses to carry passengers at the rate of fare agreed or stipulated by meter?

options.A: Permanent cancellation of licence
options.B: Fine up to Rs 500
options.C: Fine up to Rs 1,000

explanation: Section 178(3)(b) prescribes a fine which may extend to fifty rupees (Rs 50) for overcharging or refusing stipulated fare.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a ticketless passenger who refuses to pay fare under Section 178 be removed from the bus?

options.A: Only after getting a warrant from a magistrate
options.B: No, passengers have a constitutional right to remain in the bus
options.C: Only if all other passengers vote unanimously
options.D: Yes, the conductor or driver or an authorized officer may remove the passenger from the stage carriage

explanation: Under Section 178 and stage carriage rules, an unpaid passenger refusing fare can be lawfully removed from the bus.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a conductor allows a stage carriage to carry passengers in excess of registered seating capacity, which section applies alongside Section 178?

options.A: Section 196
options.B: Section 185
options.C: Section 189

explanation: Overcrowding and carrying excess passengers attracts Section 194A (Rs 200 per excess passenger).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178, 'stage carriage' refers to a vehicle carrying passengers at:

options.A: A single lump sum hire charge for the whole vehicle
options.B: Separate fares paid by or for individual passengers, either for the whole journey or for stages of the journey
options.C: Zero fare under corporate CSR

explanation: Section 2(40) defines stage carriage as carrying passengers for separate fares paid by individual passengers for stages.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Does a student travelling on a concession card without carrying the valid card commit an offence under Section 178?

options.A: No, students are immune from all transport rules
options.B: Yes, travelling without producing a valid pass or ticket on demand violates Section 178(1)
options.C: Only if the student is over 25 years old

explanation: Failure to produce a valid concession pass on demand amounts to travelling without a valid ticket/pass under Section 178(1).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 178, an inspecting officer who boards a KSRTC bus to check tickets is known as:

options.A: Weighbridge Operator
options.B: Arbitrator
options.C: Claims Officer

explanation: Ticket examination in state transport operations is performed by Checking Inspectors / Squads.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 179(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), whoever willfully disobeys any direction lawfully given by any person or authority empowered under this Act shall be punishable with:

options.A: Life ban from driving
options.B: Fine up to Rs 500
options.C: Simple warning letter
options.D: Fine which may extend to two thousand rupees (Rs 2,000)

explanation: Section 179(1) was amended in 2019 to enhance the fine for disobedience of lawful directions to up to two thousand rupees (Rs 2,000).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What was the fine for disobedience of orders under Section 179(1) prior to the 2019 Amendment?

options.A: Fine up to Rs 50
options.B: Fine up to Rs 100
options.C: Fine up to Rs 250

explanation: Prior to the 2019 Amendment, Section 179(1) provided a fine extending up to Rs 500.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 179(2), whoever obstructs any person or authority in the discharge of functions under this Act, or refuses information, is punishable with:

options.A: Fine up to Rs 10,000
options.B: Fine up to Rs 500 only
options.C: Imprisonment up to 1 year
options.D: Imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both

explanation: Section 179(2) prescribes imprisonment extending up to one month, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a truck driver physically blocks an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector from inspecting the vehicle's documents, which section applies?

options.A: Section 196
options.B: Section 178(1)
options.C: Section 180

explanation: Obstructing an officer in discharge of duties under the Act is punishable under Section 179(2).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a driver willfully fails to comply with a signal to stop given by an AMVI in uniform under Section 132, the driver is prosecuted under:

options.A: Section 206
options.B: Section 185
options.C: Section 194B

explanation: Disobedience of a lawful direction/signal to stop attracts penalty under Section 179(1).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 179(2), deliberately furnishing false information to a Motor Vehicles Inspector is punishable with:

options.A: Fine of Rs 50 only
options.B: A warning memo
options.C: Immediate confiscation of driving licence forever
options.D: Imprisonment for up to one month, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both

explanation: Furnishing false information or refusing to give information attracts imprisonment up to 1 month and/or fine up to Rs 2,000 under Section 179(2).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a person convicted under Section 179(2) for obstructing an officer also face prosecution under the Indian Penal Code (or BNS)?

options.A: Only if the vehicle is owned by the Central Government
options.B: No, the MV Act bars all other criminal proceedings
options.C: Only if the High Court Chief Justice grants permission
options.D: Yes, charges under IPC Section 186/353 (obstructing public servant / assault) can run concurrently

explanation: Prosecution under the MV Act does not bar prosecution under general criminal law (IPC / BNS) for obstructing public servants.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 179(1), refusing to follow diversion signs erected by traffic authorities during road works is punishable with:

options.A: No fine
options.B: Fine up to Rs 20,000
options.C: Imprisonment for 6 months

explanation: Disobeying lawful regulatory signs and traffic directions attracts fine up to Rs 2,000 under Section 179(1).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Is an offence under Section 179(1) compoundable by authorized officers under Section 200?

options.A: Compoundable only if the offender is a foreign citizen
options.B: No, it is strictly non-compoundable
options.C: Compoundable only by the State Transport Appellate Tribunal
options.D: Yes, it is a compoundable offence

explanation: Section 179(1) is compoundable under Section 200.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Does Section 179 apply to vehicle owners who refuse to supply information demanded under Section 133?

options.A: Only during parliamentary elections
options.B: No, Section 133 has no penal teeth
options.C: Only if demanded by an officer above the rank of RTO
options.D: Yes, refusal to supply information under Section 133 is penalized under Section 179(2)

explanation: Refusal to supply owner information required under Section 133 is prosecuted under Section 179(2).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 180 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), what is the penalty for an owner who allows an unauthorized person to drive a vehicle without a valid licence?

options.A: Imprisonment for 2 years
options.B: Fine of Rs 500 only
options.C: Fine of Rs 1,000 only
options.D: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine of five thousand rupees (Rs 5,000), or both

explanation: Section 180 prescribes imprisonment up to three months, or fine of five thousand rupees (Rs 5,000), or both.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What was the fine under Section 180 prior to the 2019 Amendment?

options.A: Rs 100
options.B: Rs 500
options.C: Rs 250

explanation: Prior to 2019, the fine under Section 180 was up to Rs 1,000.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Who is held liable under Section 180?

options.A: The person who does not have a driving licence
options.B: The owner or person in charge of a motor vehicle who causes or permits any other person who does not satisfy the provisions of Section 3 or Section 4 to drive
options.C: The driving school instructor exclusively
options.D: The RTO clerk who issued the application

explanation: Section 180 specifically holds the owner or person in charge liable for allowing an unqualified/unlicensed person to drive.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a father allows his 16-year-old son to drive his gear car on a public road, which section penalizes the father as owner?

options.A: Section 196
options.B: Section 177 only
options.C: Section 185

explanation: Allowing a person who contravenes Section 4 (age restrictions) to drive penalizes the owner under Section 180 and Section 199A.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a transport fleet owner hires a driver knowing the driver holds only a non-transport LMV licence to drive a heavy articulated truck:

options.A: The insurance company pays a reward
options.B: The owner has no liability
options.C: The driver's licence is automatically upgraded
options.D: The owner is liable under Section 180 for permitting an unauthorized driver

explanation: Allowing someone without the appropriate class of licence to drive commercial vehicles makes the owner liable under Section 180.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the compounding fee for an offence under Section 180 in Kerala?
explanation: In Kerala, Section 180 is compounded at Rs 5,000 as per statutory notification.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 180, can a person 'in charge of the vehicle' who is not the legal owner be prosecuted?

options.A: No, only the person whose name is in the RC can be prosecuted
options.B: Yes, the statute explicitly says 'the owner or person in charge of a motor vehicle'
options.C: Only if they have a power of attorney
options.D: Only if the vehicle is a government vehicle

explanation: Section 180 applies to 'the owner or other person in charge of a motor vehicle'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If an owner hands over car keys to a friend who is visibly heavily intoxicated, which sections can apply?

options.A: Section 120 only
options.B: Section 178 only
options.C: Section 114 only

explanation: Permitting an intoxicated person to drive attracts Section 180 and abetment of drunken driving under Section 188 read with Section 185.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Does a defence of 'I forgot to check their licence' protect an owner under Section 180?

options.A: Yes, ignorance is a complete defence
options.B: No, the owner has a statutory duty of due diligence to ensure the person permitted has a valid driving licence
options.C: Yes, if the friend promised they had a licence
options.D: Only if the drive was less than 5 minutes

explanation: Owners have a strict duty of due diligence before entrusting vehicles; negligence is no defence under Section 180.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What impact does a conviction under Section 180 have on third-party insurance claims?

options.A: The policy premium is refunded
options.B: The victim loses all compensation
options.C: The insurer may claim breach of policy conditions by the insured owner and seek pay-and-recover from the owner

explanation: Permitting an unlicensed driver is a fundamental breach of policy, allowing the insurer to recover the award from the owner.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019), what is the penalty for driving a motor vehicle without a valid driving licence in contravention of Section 3?

options.A: Fine of Rs 1,000 only
options.B: Fine of Rs 500 only
options.C: Imprisonment up to 3 months, or fine of five thousand rupees (Rs 5,000), or both

explanation: Section 181 prescribes imprisonment up to three months, or fine of five thousand rupees (Rs 5,000), or both.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Prior to the 2019 Amendment, what was the fine amount under Section 181?

options.A: Rs 250
options.C: Rs 500

explanation: Prior to the 2019 Amendment, the fine under Section 181 was up to Rs 500.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Section 181 penalizes driving in contravention of:

explanation: For non-transport private vehicles, Green Tax is levied at the time of 15-year registration renewal for a 5-year block.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory objective of levying Green Tax under Section 3A?

options.A: To discourage the continued use of older, polluting vehicles and generate funds to tackle environmental pollution
options.B: To subsidize luxury sports cars
options.C: To fund highway toll plazas
options.D: To replace all trees along highways

explanation: Green Tax disincentivizes older polluting vehicles and finances environmental/road safety initiatives.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Are fully electric vehicles (EVs) liable to pay Green Tax under Section 3A?

options.A: No, zero-emission electric vehicles are exempt from Green Tax
options.B: Yes, EVs pay double Green Tax
options.C: Only electric buses pay Green Tax

explanation: Zero-emission electric vehicles do not emit tailpipe pollutants and are exempt from Green Tax.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the validity period of Green Tax paid for an older transport vehicle under Section 3A in Kerala?

options.A: One year (paid annually at the time of fitness certificate renewal)
options.B: 15 years
options.C: 3 months

explanation: For transport vehicles, Green Tax is paid annually alongside the annual fitness renewal.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 3A, is Green Tax payable in addition to the normal road tax payable under Section 3?

options.A: Yes, Green Tax is levied in addition to any tax levied under Section 3
options.B: No, Green Tax replaces normal tax
options.C: Only 10% of Green Tax is payable
options.D: Green Tax is deducted from normal tax

explanation: Section 3A explicitly specifies that Green Tax is levied 'in addition to the tax leviable under Section 3'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4(1) of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, tax must be paid:

options.A: In advance, within the prescribed grace period from the commencement of the tax period
options.B: At the end of the year
options.C: Only when the vehicle is sold
options.D: Only when the vehicle is involved in an accident

explanation: Section 4(1) requires tax to be paid in advance within the prescribed period (grace period).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the standard grace period allowed under the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules for payment of quarterly tax without penalty?

options.A: 14 days (or up to 45 days as notified by Government for specific quarters)
options.B: 6 months
options.C: 1 year

explanation: The standard statutory grace period is 14 days from commencement of quarter, frequently extended up to 30 or 45 days by notification.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4(2), upon payment of tax, what document is granted to the owner?

options.A: A tax licence (or digital tax receipt / tax token) in the prescribed form
options.B: A commercial trade licence
options.C: A free toll pass

explanation: Section 4(2) provides that the Taxation Officer shall issue a tax licence in the prescribed form.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4, what happens to the tax licence when a motor vehicle is used in a public place?

options.A: The tax licence or receipt must be carried in the vehicle or verifiable electronically through Vahan
options.B: It must be deposited in the district court
options.C: It must be framed at home
options.D: It must be mailed to the Governor

explanation: Tax payment proof must be available for inspection in physical or digital form (Vahan/mParivahan).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4, can road tax in Kerala be paid online?

options.A: Yes, through the Parivahan / e-Payment portal of the Motor Vehicles Department
options.B: No, tax can only be paid in gold coins at the Secretariat
options.C: Only cash payments at local post offices are permitted
options.D: Only cheques drawn on foreign banks are accepted

explanation: Modern tax collection is fully automated online via the national Parivahan portal.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 4(1), who is primarily responsible for the payment of tax?

options.A: The registered owner or the person having possession or control of the motor vehicle
options.B: The tyre manufacturer
options.C: The fuel pump operator

explanation: The registered owner or person having possession/control is statutorily liable to pay the tax.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 5(1) of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, what is the procedure to obtain tax exemption when a vehicle is NOT in use?

options.A: The owner must file a prior intimation of non-use in Form G to the Taxation Officer before the commencement of the quarter/period
options.B: The owner can simply stop paying tax without telling anyone
options.C: The owner can send a WhatsApp text after 6 months
options.D: The owner can dismantle the engine without notice

explanation: Section 5(1) requires prior filing of non-use application in Form G before commencement of the period.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory form used for intimation of non-use under Rule 10 of Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules?

options.A: Form G
options.B: Form 20
options.C: Form B

explanation: Form G is the prescribed statutory form for claiming tax exemption due to non-use.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 5, what must the owner specify in Form G regarding the non-use of the vehicle?

options.A: The exact place where the vehicle is garaged, the period of non-use, and the reasons for non-use
options.B: The owner's bank balance
options.C: The names of all relatives
options.D: The cost of next year's tyres

explanation: Form G requires specifying the garaging location, period of non-use, and reasons (e.g. major mechanical repair).

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector inspect the garaged vehicle to verify the genuineness of Form G non-use?

options.A: Yes, physical verification of the vehicle at the declared garage is a routine duty of inspecting officers (AMVI/MVI)
options.B: No, officers are legally prohibited from inspecting garaged vehicles
options.C: Only if the vehicle caught fire
options.D: Only with a search warrant from the High Court

explanation: AMVIs conduct physical inspection of the garage to ensure the vehicle is genuinely not in use.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a vehicle for which Form G non-use exemption was claimed is caught plying on a public road during the exemption period:

options.A: The exemption is revoked, and full tax along with maximum penalty and legal prosecution is initiated
options.B: The driver receives a discount
options.C: The vehicle is declared an ambulance
options.D: No action can be taken because Form G was filed

explanation: Plying during Form G non-use constitutes tax fraud, attracting full tax, heavy penalties under Section 12, and detention.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the maximum period of non-use exemption that can be granted on a single Form G application?

options.A: Up to six months (or one year as prescribed under rules, subject to extension on fresh application)
options.B: 100 years
options.C: 1 day only

explanation: Non-use is granted for specified quarters (normally up to 6 months/1 year) and requires fresh application for further periods.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 5(2), who is empowered to grant exemption from payment of tax to any class of vehicles in public interest?

options.A: The State Government, by notification in the Gazette
options.B: Any traffic police constable
options.C: The vehicle insurance surveyor

explanation: Section 5(2) empowers the State Government to exempt any vehicle or class of vehicles from tax by notification.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Which vehicles are granted statutory or notified exemption from road tax under Section 5 in Kerala?

options.A: Agricultural tractors and power tillers used solely for agricultural purposes, and adapted vehicles of disabled persons
options.B: All luxury private sports cars
options.C: All commercial multi-axle freight trucks

explanation: Agricultural tractors used solely for farming and adapted vehicles used by disabled persons are exempt.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 6 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, when is an owner entitled to a refund of road tax?

options.A: When tax has been paid in advance and the vehicle has not been used on public roads for a continuous period of not less than one whole calendar month
options.B: Whenever petrol prices increase
options.C: If the vehicle travels less than 1,000 km in a year
options.D: If the owner moves to another house in the same town

explanation: Section 6 provides for refund where tax was paid in advance and the vehicle was not used for one or more full calendar months.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 6, what is the minimum continuous period of non-use required to claim a refund of tax?

options.A: One whole calendar month
options.B: 1 day
options.C: 7 days

explanation: Section 6 explicitly specifies non-use for 'a continuous period of not less than one whole calendar month'.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What MUST the owner surrender to the Taxation Officer to claim a tax refund under Section 6?

options.A: The tax licence / token and certificate of registration, along with proof of non-use
options.B: The vehicle steering wheel
options.C: The vehicle keys to the driver

explanation: Under Section 6 and Rule 14, the tax licence and RC must be surrendered to establish continuous non-use.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can a partial refund of one-time tax (15-year tax) be claimed if a private car is permanently removed from Kerala to another State?

options.A: Yes, pro-rata refund for the unexpired balance of the 15-year period is admissible under Section 6 and the Schedule
options.B: No, one-time tax is completely non-refundable under all circumstances
options.C: Only if the new state has zero road tax

explanation: When a vehicle is permanently removed on change of address to another state, pro-rata refund for unexpired quarters is admissible.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 6, within what time from the expiry of the period must an application for refund be submitted?

options.A: Within the prescribed time limit (normally within 3 months / 6 months of expiry of period)
options.B: Within 20 years
options.C: Within 24 hours only

explanation: Refund applications must be filed within the prescribed statutory limitation period under KMV Taxation Rules.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 7 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, when does liability to pay 'Additional Tax' arise?

options.A: When a motor vehicle is altered or used in a manner that causes it to become liable to tax at a higher rate than what was paid
options.B: When the vehicle is washed with shampoo
options.C: When the driver changes clothes
options.D: When the car travels into another district

explanation: Section 7 mandates additional tax when vehicle alterations or usage changes push it into a higher tax bracket.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If an educational institution bus paying concessional tax is used on weekends as a commercial contract carriage carrying tourists:

options.A: Additional tax under Section 7 is payable at the contract carriage rate for the relevant period
options.B: No extra tax is payable
options.C: The vehicle is immediately demolished

explanation: Changing use to a higher-rated commercial contract carriage triggers additional tax liability under Section 7.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If a truck's seating capacity or registered laden weight is increased by structural alteration, the owner must pay additional tax under:

options.A: Section 7
options.B: Section 2(e)
options.C: Section 26 only

explanation: Increasing GVW increases the tax slab, requiring additional tax under Section 7.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 7, how is the additional tax calculated?

options.A: The difference between the tax payable at the higher rate and the tax already paid for the unexpired portion of the period
options.B: Double the entire purchase value of the vehicle
options.C: A flat fee of Rs 50
options.D: Triple the annual budget of the RTO

explanation: Section 7 specifies payment of an additional tax of a sum equal to the difference between higher tax and tax already paid.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 10 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, who is empowered to stop a motor vehicle in any public place?

options.A: Any Officer of the Police or Motor Vehicles Department not below the prescribed rank
options.B: Any toll booth cashier
options.C: Any private bus conductor

explanation: Section 10 empowers officers of Police or Motor Vehicles Department not below prescribed rank (AMVI and above) to stop vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the purpose of stopping a vehicle under Section 10?

options.A: To inspect the tax licence or satisfy themselves that tax has been paid in respect of the vehicle
options.B: To collect personal donations
options.C: To borrow petrol from the tank

explanation: The statutory purpose under Section 10 is checking tax licences and verifying payment of tax under the Act.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 10, what is the duty of the driver when signaled to stop by an AMVI in uniform?

options.A: The driver shall immediately stop the vehicle and keep it stationary until the officer permits him to proceed
options.B: The driver should accelerate and escape
options.C: The driver should switch off lights and honk
options.D: The driver has no obligation to stop

explanation: Section 10 mandates that the driver shall stop and remain stationary until permitted to proceed.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 11 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, an authorized officer may seize and detain a motor vehicle if:

options.A: The tax due in respect of the vehicle has not been paid within the prescribed time
options.B: The vehicle is older than 3 years
options.C: The driver does not carry an ATM card

explanation: Section 11 empowers authorized officers to seize and detain vehicles in respect of which tax has not been paid.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 11, for how long can a vehicle seized for tax default be detained in custody?

options.A: Until the tax due, together with penalty and custody charges, is fully paid
options.B: Strictly 2 hours only
options.C: Forever without remedy

explanation: The vehicle remains detained under Section 11 until all tax arrears, penalties, and custody expenses are satisfied.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 11, if the tax and penalty remain unpaid after due notice, what power does the Taxation Officer have?

options.A: Power to sell the motor vehicle by public auction to recover the tax arrears and expenses
options.B: Power to give the vehicle to his relatives
options.C: Power to push the vehicle into the sea
options.D: Power to dismantle the vehicle for scrap without public auction

explanation: Section 11 authorizes selling the detained motor vehicle in public auction to recover outstanding dues.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Can an Assistant Motor Vehicles Inspector in Kerala seize a commercial bus for default of quarterly road tax under Section 11?

options.A: Yes, AMVIs are authorized officers under notifications issued under Section 11
options.B: No, only the District Judge can seize vehicles
options.C: Only if the bus is registered in another country
options.D: Only if the bus has no passengers

explanation: AMVIs and MVIs are designated authorized officers under Section 11 to seize and detain tax-defaulting vehicles.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 12 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, what is payable when tax is not paid within the prescribed due date?

options.A: Additional tax by way of penalty (penal interest/penalty at prescribed percentage slabs)
options.B: Only a verbal warning
options.C: A lottery ticket

explanation: Section 12 prescribes additional tax by way of penalty for default in payment of tax within the due date.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Rules, what is the maximum penalty percentage leviable under Section 12 for prolonged tax default?

options.A: Up to 50% (or 100% of the tax due depending on the duration of default exceeding six months)
options.B: 1% flat
options.C: 5% flat

explanation: Penalties under Section 12 are graduated based on duration of default, reaching up to 50% or 100% of the tax due.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 12, can the Taxation Officer waive the penalty if sufficient cause is shown for non-payment?

options.A: Yes, if the officer is satisfied that the failure was due to circumstances beyond control and not willful neglect
options.B: No, the officer has zero discretion under any circumstances
options.C: Only if the owner pays a private fee

explanation: Under prescribed rules and Section 12, penalty may be mitigated/waived on proof of genuine unavoidable circumstances.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 13 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, any amount due on account of tax, penalty, or interest may be recovered:

options.A: As arrears of land revenue under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act, 1968
options.B: Through private recovery bouncers
options.C: By deducting salary of the AMVI
options.D: By seizing the vehicle driver's school certificates

explanation: Section 13 explicitly provides that tax, penalty, and interest are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What powers are available under the Revenue Recovery (RR) Act when tax arrears are recovered under Section 13?

options.A: Attachment and sale of movable and immovable properties of the defaulting owner, and arrest/detention in civil jail in case of fraudulent evasion
options.B: Publishing photos on highway banners only
options.C: Denying telephone connections

explanation: Revenue recovery proceedings under Section 13 enable attachment and sale of immovable land/buildings and movable assets.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Does the recovery of tax under Section 13 bar the department from also seizing the vehicle under Section 11?

options.A: No, remedies under Section 11 (seizure of vehicle) and Section 13 (revenue recovery) are concurrent and cumulative until tax is satisfied
options.B: Yes, only one remedy can be chosen
options.C: Seizure of vehicle is illegal once RR notice is issued
options.D: RR proceedings can only be initiated after vehicle is auctioned

explanation: The departmental remedies of vehicle detention and revenue recovery operate concurrently to secure public revenue.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 26 of the Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976, 'escaped assessment' empowers the Taxation Officer to:

options.A: Assess or re-assess tax that has escaped assessment or has been under-assessed within the prescribed limitation period
options.B: Forgive all past taxes forever
options.C: Double the tax arbitrarily without notice

explanation: Section 26 gives power to assess or re-assess tax which has escaped assessment or was assessed at too low a rate.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: Under Section 26, before making an assessment of escaped tax, what MUST the Taxation Officer serve on the owner?

options.A: A notice giving the owner a reasonable opportunity of being heard (show-cause notice)
options.B: An immediate arrest warrant
options.C: A demand for cash deposit within 1 hour
options.D: A demolition notice for the vehicle

explanation: Section 26 requires issuing a notice to the owner and affording a reasonable opportunity of showing cause.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: What is the statutory limitation period for reopening an escaped assessment under Section 26?

options.A: Within four (4) years from the end of the year to which the tax relates
options.B: Within 30 days only
options.C: Within 50 years

explanation: Section 26 specifies a limitation period of four years from the end of the relevant tax year.

subject: JOB RELATED TOPICS
question: If an owner registers a luxury car in Puducherry using fake address documents to evade high Kerala road tax, can Kerala MVD assess escaped tax under Section 26?

options.A: Yes, if the vehicle is kept or used in Kerala, tax can be assessed under Section 3 read with Section 26 along with penalties
options.B: No, Puducherry registration grants absolute permanent immunity in Kerala
options.C: Only if the owner is arrested by Puducherry police
options.D: Kerala has no jurisdiction over vehicles with PY registration

explanation: Under Section 3 and Section 26, vehicles kept or used in Kerala are subject to Kerala tax regardless of fraudulent outside registration.

subject: AMVI
question: Output of alternators employed in automobile electrical system is regulated by a:

options.A: Cutout relay
options.B: Current regulator
options.C: Voltage regulator

explanation: In an automotive alternator charging system, the output voltage is regulated by a voltage regulator (electromechanical or solid-state electronic IC). A current regulator is not required because an alternator has natural self-limiting current characteristics due to stator inductive reactance, and built-in diodes prevent reverse discharge.

subject: AMVI
question: The resilience of a material id considered when it is subjected to :

options.A: shock loading
options.B: fatigue
options.C: creep

explanation: Resilience is the mechanical property of a material to absorb energy when deformed elastically and release that energy upon unloading without permanent deformation. It is the primary design consideration for components subject to impact and shock loading (e.g. suspension springs).

subject: AMVI
question: Which gearbox uses synchronizing unit?

options.A: Synchromesh gear box
options.B: Constant mesh gear box
options.C: Sliding mesh gear box

explanation: A synchromesh gearbox incorporates synchronizing cone clutches and dog teeth units to equalize the rotational speeds of the gear and the mainshaft before engagement, eliminating the need for double-declutching and preventing gear clashing.

subject: AMVI
question: Pulsation of clutch pedal is due to :

options.A: Loose Rivets
options.B: Misalignment of engine and transmission
options.C: Worn out clutch facing

explanation: Pulsation or vibration felt in the clutch pedal during initial depression is commonly caused by mechanical angular or parallel misalignment between the engine crankshaft axis and the transmission input shaft, or by unevenly adjusted clutch release levers.

subject: AMVI
question: Test conducted on injector are:

options.A: Pressure test.
options.B: Leak off test.
options.C: Spray test.

explanation: Standard workshop tests performed on a diesel fuel injector nozzle using a nozzle tester include: (1) Opening pressure test (pop-up pressure setting), (2) Leak-off test (checking clearance leakage between nozzle needle and body), (3) Spray pattern test (atomization and cone angle), and (4) Chatter / drippiness test.

subject: AMVI
question: Circumferential grooves on automobile

options.A: Provide good traction
options.B: Reduce the danger of skidding
options.C: Prevent small stones sticking to the tyre

explanation: Circumferential grooves running around the perimeter of automotive tyre treads provide open channels for expelling water rapidly from beneath the tyre contact patch, preventing hydroplaning (aquaplaning) and reducing the danger of lateral skidding on wet roads.

subject: AMVI
question: Super elevation is .......... of a horizontal curved portion of a road

options.A: Convexity
options.B: Inward transverse inclination
options.C: Positive grade

explanation: Super-elevation (banking) in road geometry is the inward transverse inclination provided to the outer edge of a highway pavement across a horizontal curve, elevating the outer edge above the inner edge to counteract the overturning and outward skidding tendencies caused by centrifugal force.

subject: AMVI
question: Excessive clutch free pedal play would cause:

options.A: Clutch rattle
options.B: Clutch slip
options.C: Torsional vibration

explanation: Excessive clutch pedal free play means the clutch release bearing does not travel far enough when the pedal is depressed to the floor. Consequently, the pressure plate does not fully release the driven plate, causing clutch drag and difficult gear shifting.

subject: AMVI
question: Aerodynamic drag on a vehicle is experienced most when the vehicle:

options.A: is moving at low speed
options.B: is moving at high speed
options.C: is moving reverse direction

explanation: Aerodynamic drag force is proportional to the square of vehicle speed: Fd = 1/2 * rho * Cd * A * v^2. At low speeds, rolling resistance dominates, but at high cruising speeds, aerodynamic drag becomes the single largest resistance opposing vehicle motion.

subject: AMVI
question: A.C. mechanical fuel pump tests are;

options.A: pressure test
options.B: Volume test
options.C: Vaccum test

explanation: The standard shop tests for an A.C. mechanical diaphragm fuel pump include: (1) Pressure test (checking fuel delivery pressure, typically 0.2 to 0.35 bar), (2) Volume test (checking fuel discharge volume per minute/strokes), and (3) Vacuum test (checking the suction created at the inlet).

subject: AMVI
question: Example of multi grade oil is:

options.A: SAE20
options.B: SAE30

explanation: SAE 20W-40 (or SAE 20-40) is a multigrade engine oil formulated with viscosity index improvers so that it behaves like a thin SAE 20 oil at low temperatures for easy cold starting, while retaining the lubricating film strength of an SAE 40 oil at high engine operating temperatures.

subject: AMVI
question: A manual method commonly used for measuring the engine lubricating oil level is

options.A: An oil level indicator
options.B: An oil pressure gauge
options.C: An oil dipstick

explanation: An engine oil dipstick is the universal manual workshop tool used to measure the static lubricating oil level in the engine crankcase sump, featuring engraved 'MAX' and 'MIN' level marks.

subject: AMVI
question: Cylinder block construction by mono-block is preferred to individual cylinder construction because of:

options.A: Compact engine size
options.B: Easy manufacturing operations
options.C: Better water sealed joints

explanation: Monoblock cylinder block construction (casting all cylinders together in a single rigid block) offers compact overall engine dimensions, streamlined mass production, higher structural rigidity, and eliminates problematic water-jacket sealing joints between separate cylinders.

subject: AMVI
question: The standard firing order of a six cylinder in-line left hand crank shaft is:
explanation: The standard and most universally adopted firing order for a six-cylinder in-line four-stroke automotive engine is 1 - 5 - 3 - 6 - 2 - 4, which ensures optimal dynamic balance and evenly distributed bearing loads along the crankshaft.

subject: AMVI
question: The purpose of circumferential fins constructed on the outer periphery of the brake drum is to:

options.A: Reduce the weight of the drum
options.B: Reduce the brake noise
options.C: Guarantee uniform intensity of pressure

explanation: Circumferential cooling fins cast onto the external outer periphery of heavy-duty brake drums increase the effective surface area exposed to ambient airflow, enhancing convective heat dissipation and significantly lowering brake operating temperatures to prevent brake fade.

subject: AMVI
question: EBD is a .............. device in modern vehicle

options.A: Brake assistance
options.B: Stability programme
options.C: Electronic ignition

explanation: EBD stands for Electronic Brakeforce Distribution, an active brake safety assistance system that works in conjunction with ABS to automatically vary the proportion of braking force applied to each individual wheel based on dynamic load conditions and available road grip.

subject: AMVI
question: The part of a torque converter that facilitates change of torque between input and Output shafts is the:

options.A: Turbine
options.B: Impeller
options.C: Stator

explanation: A hydraulic torque converter contains three main elements: the engine-driven impeller (pump), the output turbine, and the stationary stator (reactor). The stator redirects the fluid returning from the turbine back into the impeller in the direction of rotation, multiplying engine torque.

subject: AMVI
question: Odometer is used to measure:

options.A: Speed
options.B: Temperature
options.C: Pressure

explanation: An odometer is an instrument integrated into the vehicle dashboard instrument cluster that records and displays the total cumulative distance traveled by the vehicle in kilometres or miles.

subject: AMVI
question: Which thermodynamic law provide the basis of temperature measurement ?

options.A: I law of thermodynamics
options.B: II law of thermodynamics
options.C: Law of conservation of energy

explanation: The Zeroth Law of Thermodynamics states that if two thermodynamic systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other. This principle provides the foundational physical basis for temperature measurement and thermometers.

subject: AMVI
question: In a Mac Pherson strut type of independent suspension, the coil spring is arranged:

options.A: Between the lower wish bone and the cross member
options.B: Between the lower wish bone and the strut
options.C: Between the strut and the cross member
options.D: On a strut carrying the shock absorber

explanation: In a MacPherson strut independent front suspension, the coil spring is concentrically mounted directly on the telescopic structural strut that encloses the hydraulic shock absorber (damper), forming a compact integrated suspension unit.

subject: AMVI
question: Crumbling zone:

options.A: Structural region designed to collapse in a crash-absorbing energy
options.B: Energy absorbing bumber
options.C: Crumbling roof of car

explanation: A crumple zone (crumbling zone) is a structural section at the front and rear of a vehicle's body designed to progressively deform, buckle, and crush during a crash, thereby absorbing impact energy and decelerating the passenger cabin safely.

subject: AMVI
question: The advantage of hypoid gear final drive over spiral bevel gear final drive is

options.A: Propeller shaft can be positioned up or down
options.B: Good contact
options.C: Easy overhaul

explanation: The hypoid gear final drive has its pinion axis offset below (or above) the center line of the crown wheel. This offset lowers the propeller shaft line, allowing vehicle manufacturers to lower the floor line and center of gravity of the passenger cabin without needing a large transmission tunnel.

subject: AMVI
question: Purpose of thermostat valve is;

options.A: Allow engine to attain working temperature
options.B: Indicate fuel level
options.C: Prevent boiling of coolant

explanation: The thermostat valve in an engine water cooling system prevents coolant from flowing to the radiator when the engine is cold, recirculating it within the cylinder block and head until the engine rapidly attains its optimum operating temperature (typically 80°C to 90°C).

subject: AMVI
question: The term 'clutch slip' as applied to a fluid flywheel:

options.A: Decreases with the speed of driving shaft
options.B: Increases with the speed of driving shaft
options.C: Remains steady at all speeds of the driving shaft
options.D: Remains steady at all speeds of the driven shaft

explanation: In a fluid flywheel (fluid coupling), 'clutch slip' is the difference in rotational speed between the driving impeller and the driven runner. At engine idle speed, slip is nearly 100% (zero torque transmission), but as the driving shaft speed increases, centrifugal fluid circulation increases and slip decreases to around 2-3% at cruising speeds.

subject: AMVI
question: All types of live axles have to take:

options.A: Torque reaction
options.B: Driving torque
options.C: Weight of the vehicle

explanation: All live axles (semi-floating, three-quarter floating, and full-floating) transmit driving torque to the road wheels. However, in a full-floating axle, the axle casing carries the vehicle weight and bending loads, so the axle shaft itself takes only driving torque.

subject: AMVI
question: Expansion tank is employed in .......... system

options.A: Fuel
options.B: Lubrication
options.C: Cooling

explanation: An expansion tank (coolant recovery reservoir) is an integral component of a closed liquid engine cooling system that provides space for the thermal expansion and contraction of engine coolant as its temperature fluctuates.

subject: AMVI
question: Heat dam is cut in

options.A: Crown
options.B: Skirt
options.C: Ring groove

explanation: A heat dam is a narrow circumferential groove cut into the top land of the piston above the top compression ring groove. It restricts the conduction of intense combustion heat from the piston crown down to the compression rings, protecting the rings from sticking.

subject: AMVI
question: Which is not the common component between a petrol and a diesel engine?

options.A: Dynamo
options.B: Fuel pump
options.C: Tail pipe

explanation: An ignition coil is present in a petrol (Spark Ignition) engine to generate the high voltage spark across spark plugs. Diesel (Compression Ignition) engines rely on the heat of compression to ignite the fuel spray and do not use an ignition coil.

subject: AMVI
question: Volumetric efficiency of an engine is increased by :

options.A: Using large inlet value
options.B: Using more number of piston rings
options.C: Increasing gap between head and piston

explanation: Volumetric efficiency is directly governed by breathing resistance. Using a larger-diameter inlet valve (or multiple intake valves per cylinder) increases the cross-sectional intake flow area, decreases throttling losses, and admits a greater mass of air-fuel mixture into the cylinder.

subject: AMVI
question: As per the section IV of Motor Vehicle Act 1988, the minimum age limit for obtaining a driving licence to drive a transport vehicle is:

options.A: 16 years
options.B: 18 years
options.C: 20 years

explanation: Under Section 4(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, no person under the age of twenty (20) years shall drive a transport vehicle in any public place.

subject: AMVI
question: The principal use of an engine dynamometer is to measure:

options.A: Torque developed by the engine
options.B: Power developed by the engine
options.C: Thermal efficiency of the engine
options.D: Net work done by the engine

explanation: An engine dynamometer (such as a hydraulic, eddy-current, or prony brake dynamometer) primarily measures the braking torque (T) developed by the engine output shaft at a known rotational speed (N), from which the Brake Power (BP = 2 * pi * N * T / 60) is computed.

subject: AMVI
question: Reference fuels used for cetane rating of CI engines fuels would include:

options.A: Cetane and n-heptane
options.B: Cetane and iso-octane
options.C: Cetane and tetra ethyl lead

explanation: The reference fuels used for determining the Cetane rating of diesel fuels are: pure Cetane (n-hexadecane, assigned a rating of 100) and alpha-methyl naphthalene (assigned a rating of 0, or heptamethylnonane assigned 15).

subject: AMVI
question: Engine is a mechanical device which convert

options.A: Heat energy into mechanical energy
options.B: Mechanical energy into heat energy
options.C: Electrical energy into mechanical energy

explanation: A heat engine is a machine or mechanical device that converts the thermal (heat) energy released from the combustion of fuel into mechanical work or kinetic energy.

subject: AMVI
question: Forces acting on rear axle:

options.A: Weight of the body
options.B: Side thrust
options.C: Driving torque

explanation: The rear live axle of an automobile is subjected to multiple structural forces: vertical vehicle weight and dynamic shock loads, lateral side thrust (cornering forces), and driving torque / braking torque reaction.

subject: AMVI
question: Specific heat is the amount of heat required to rise the temperature :

options.A: By unit degree of a substance
options.B: By unit degree of unit mass of substance
options.C: Unit mass by 10 degree

explanation: Specific heat capacity (c) of a substance is defined as the quantity of heat energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of the substance by one unit degree of temperature (Q = m * c * delta_T).

subject: AMVI
question: Speed limit is included in :

options.A: Informatory sign
options.B: Cautionary sign
options.C: Road marking

explanation: A speed limit sign (a circular traffic sign featuring a red circular border enclosing black numerals indicating speed on a white background) is classified under the Motor Vehicles Act as a Mandatory (Regulatory) traffic sign, which must be strictly obeyed by all drivers.

subject: AMVI
question: Brake caliper is :

options.A: used in disc brakes
options.B: used for measuring brake pad thickness
options.C: used for brake setting

explanation: In an automotive disc brake assembly, the brake caliper is the housing that straddles the brake disc rotor, accommodating the hydraulic pistons and clamping the friction brake pads against the spinning disc faces.

subject: AMVI
question: Materials having same elastic properties in all directions is called :

options.A: Isentropic material
options.B: Uniform material
options.C: Elastic material

explanation: An isotropic material (noted as 'Isentropic material' in historical question prints) is an ideal engineering material that exhibits identical elastic and physical properties (modulus of elasticity, Poisson's ratio, etc.) in all directions at any point.

subject: AMVI
question: One liter of water occupies a volume of :

options.A: 100\text{ cm}^3
options.C: 1000\text{ cm}^3

explanation: One litre of pure water occupies a volume of exactly 1,000 cubic centimetres (1,000 cm^3 or 1 cubic decimetre = 10^-3 m^3).

subject: AMVI
question: An engine has clearance volume by 10 CC and swept volume is 70 CC. The compression ratio is:
explanation: Compression Ratio (r) is calculated as: r = (Vs + Vc) / Vc. Given swept volume Vs = 70 cc and clearance volume Vc = 10 cc: r = (70 + 10) / 10 = 80 / 10 = 8:1.

subject: AMVI
question: A high viscosity index of lubricating oil indicates:

options.A: Relatively little change of viscosity with change of pressure
options.B: Relatively large change of viscosity with change of pressure
options.C: Relatively little change of viscosity with change of temperature
options.D: Relatively large change of viscosity with change of temperature

explanation: A high Viscosity Index (VI) indicates that the lubricating oil exhibits relatively little change in its dynamic viscosity across wide changes in operating temperature, ensuring fluid lubrication during cold morning starting and maintaining protective film thickness at high engine loads.

subject: AMVI
question: The testing and adjustment of a diesel injection pump for the accuracy of its firing interval is known as:

options.A: Calibration
options.B: Governing
options.C: Phasing

explanation: Phasing is the shop testing and adjustment of a multi-cylinder diesel inline fuel injection pump to ensure that the start of fuel delivery from each pumping element occurs at precisely the correct angular intervals (e.g. exactly 90° apart on a 4-cylinder pump, 60° on a 6-cylinder pump). Calibration ensures equal delivery quantity.

subject: AMVI
question: The purpose of a condenser in the ignition system of a petrol engine is to:

options.A: Regulate current produced by the dynamo
options.B: Step-up the primary voltage
options.C: Avoid arcing across the contact breaker points
options.D: Distribute high voltage to the engine cylinder according to the firing order

explanation: The ignition condenser (capacitor) connected across the contact breaker points absorbs the primary back-EMF when the points open, preventing electrical arcing across the gap, thereby ensuring rapid collapse of the primary magnetic field and protecting the points from burning.

subject: AMVI
question: Viscous coupling is employed instead of ............ in modern vehicles

options.A: Steering
options.B: Differential
options.C: Brake

explanation: In modern all-wheel-drive (AWD) vehicles, a viscous coupling unit (containing interleaved slotted plates immersed in high-viscosity silicone fluid) is employed in place of a conventional mechanical center differential to smoothly transfer torque between front and rear axles during wheel slip.

subject: AMVI
question: FFV stands for :

options.A: Flexi fuel vehicle
options.B: Fuel free vehicle
options.C: Fully forward vehicle

explanation: FFV stands for Flex-Fuel Vehicle (Flexible-Fuel Vehicle), which is an alternative-fuel automobile equipped with an internal combustion engine capable of operating on gasoline blended with varying percentages of ethanol or methanol (up to 85% or 100%).

subject: AMVI
question: In case of offset pistons, the piston pin hole axis is made offset from the cylinder centreline towards the:

options.A: Major thrust side
options.B: Minor thrust side
options.C: Major or minor thrust side

explanation: In offset pistons, the piston pin bore axis is offset slightly (typically 1 mm to 1.5 mm) from the cylinder centerline towards the major thrust side (the side supporting connecting rod angle during the power stroke) to minimize piston slap.

subject: AMVI
question: Important properties of lubricating oil:

options.A: Viscosity.
options.B: physical stability.
options.C: Chemical stability.

explanation: The essential functional properties required of an automotive lubricating oil include: proper viscosity and high viscosity index, physical stability (resistance to foaming, low pour point, high flash point), and chemical stability (resistance to thermal oxidation, corrosion, and sludge formation).

subject: AMVI
question: Slip angle is:

options.A: Angle between the two front wheel direction
options.B: Angle between King pin centre line and Wheel centre line
options.C: Angle between direction of travel of car and direction in which tyre is pointing

explanation: Slip angle is the angular difference between the actual direction of travel of the vehicle (the wheel heading) and the longitudinal plane in which the tyre is pointing when subject to lateral cornering forces.

subject: AMVI
question: In an alternator, the electromotive force is induced in the:

options.A: Stator windings
options.B: Rotor windings
options.C: Damper windings

explanation: In an automotive alternator, the alternating electromotive force (AC voltage) is induced in the stationary three-phase stator windings as the rotating magnetic field produced by the DC-excited rotor passes across them.

subject: AMVI
question: Specific gravity of a lubricating oil can be determined by a:

options.A: Rota meter
options.B: Orifice meter
options.C: Anemo meter

explanation: The specific gravity of liquid petroleum products and lubricating oils is measured using a hydrometer (or pycnometer) calibrated for liquid density measurement.

subject: AMVI
question: A.C Mechanical pump is employed in :

options.A: Fuel system
options.B: Automatic transmission system
options.C: Air conditioning

explanation: An A.C. mechanical pump (AC diaphragm fuel pump) is an engine-driven positive-displacement pump actuated by an eccentric cam on the engine camshaft to draw fuel from the petrol tank and supply it to the carburettor in older IC engines.

subject: AMVI
question: Volumetric efficiency is the ratio of :

options.A: Volume of charge admitted at NTP to swept volume
options.B: Total volume to clearance volume
options.C: Swept volume to clearance volume

explanation: Volumetric efficiency (eta_v) of an internal combustion engine is the ratio of the actual mass (or volume reduced to Normal Temperature and Pressure - NTP) of fresh air-fuel mixture or air drawn into the cylinder during the intake stroke to the theoretical swept volume of the cylinder.

subject: AMVI
question: The Motor vehicle to which semi- trailer is attached is called :

options.A: Tractor
options.B: Grader
options.C: Articulated vehicle

explanation: Under Section 2(2) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, a motor vehicle to which a semi-trailer is attached (comprising a prime mover tractor unit articulated with a trailing semi-trailer) is defined as an 'Articulated Vehicle'.

subject: AMVI
question: The type of gears used for transmitting power between two non-intersecting perpendicular shafts is

options.A: Hypoid gears
options.B: Straight bevel gears
options.C: Spiral bevel gears

explanation: Hypoid bevel gears are specialized spiral bevel gears where the axes of the driving pinion and driven crown wheel are non-intersecting and perpendicular, allowing the pinion shaft to be offset below the center of the ring gear.

subject: AMVI
question: Knocking tendency in a SI engine reduces with increasing:

options.A: Engine speed
options.B: Compression ratio
options.C: Supercharging

explanation: In a Spark Ignition engine, increasing engine speed increases in-cylinder charge turbulence and flame propagation speed, significantly reducing the residence time available for the unburned end gas to reach its self-ignition temperature, thereby reducing the knocking tendency.

subject: AMVI
question: The following is not a part of secondary side of ignition system;

options.A: Spark plug
options.B: Distributor rotor
options.C: Secondary side of ignition coil

explanation: In a battery ignition system, the contact breaker (CB) points are connected in the low-voltage primary circuit (12 V) in series with the primary winding. The secondary high-voltage circuit consists of the secondary winding, distributor rotor, distributor cap, high-tension cables, and spark plugs.

subject: AMVI
question: Wankel engine is a

options.A: Reciprocating engine
options.B: Rotary engine
options.C: Electric generator

explanation: The Wankel engine is a rotary internal combustion engine that uses an eccentric rotary design (a triangular Reuleaux rotor orbiting inside an epitrochoidal housing) instead of reciprocating pistons to convert thermal energy directly into rotational motion.

subject: AMVI
question: A wet clutch is more preferred to a dry clutch:

options.A: When it is desired to disengage the clutch speedily
options.B: When it is desired to transmit large amount of torque effectively
options.C: When it is desired to achieve longer life
